   provenance needed to locate the source remittance.
2. A hold transition calls it again with the new state.
3. With NO receiver registered, every behaviour is unchanged and no error is
   logged as a failure.
4. A receiver that raises does not change the hold, the claim, the ledger or
   anything the practice sees; the failure is logged and the path continues.
5. A receiver that blocks does not block the posting path.
6. The engine imports no implementation of the protocol.
7. make check passes.
notes: REWRITTEN 2026-09-10. This bead used to say the engine should keep the remittance as an evidence corpus. Kurt's call: working out WHY the numbers disagreed belongs outside the engine, so the engine offers a seam and holds no corpus. The receiver that does the investigating is tracked separately, off this board.

title: Never bill a client from a remittance that contradicts itself
description:
A payer states the client's share of a claim twice in one remittance — once as
a claim total (CLP05) and again itemised across the service lines as PR-group
adjustments. When those two disagree, the engine currently believes the total
and bills the client on it.

app/claims/remittance_lines.py:146 patient_responsibility_agrees() already
detects the disagreement and has zero production callers. Downstream,
apply_posting writes a row on the client's ledger regardless.

This epic makes the engine hold the client's bill instead: post what the payer
paid, withhold the client's ledger row, record the disagreement, and put it in
front of the clinician who owns the claim with two answers they can give
without waiting for anyone — bill it as stated, or waive it.

The practice does the deciding. They hold the client relationship and the
authority over that balance; the software's job is to say what it found and to
refuse to guess.
design:
Three children, deliberately file-disjoint so they can run in parallel:

- PABLO-4aaq: the check on the posting path, the hold row, the withheld ledger
  write. Per-tenant table; model + migration + template regen ship together.
- PABLO-gjrj: the clinician surface and the two resolutions, extending the
  existing claim-reminder machinery (app/claims/events.py already carries an
  unmatched_remittance kind) rather than inventing a parallel surface.
- PABLO-50m3: a structured hold event re-emitted on every scheduled tick for
  every open hold, plus a heartbeat line emitted even when nothing is open.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- The payer's payment always posts. Only the client's ledger row is withheld.
- Never auto-release a hold; time passing is not evidence the number is right.
- A hold is a row with a state and timestamps, never a log line or a flag.
- Emission severity is NOTICE, never ERROR. A hold is an expected event.
- Where the events GO is per-deployment configuration. This engine emits; it
  does not route, and it names no particular recipient.
- No PHI in the emitted events.

The heartbeat-when-empty is not redundancy: a reader notices a missing line
long before it notices a missing alert, and its absence is the only signal
that the whole mechanism has stopped working during a quiet period.
acceptance_criteria:
1. PABLO-4aaq, PABLO-gjrj and PABLO-50m3 are closed.
2. A self-hosted deployment meeting a self-contradicting remittance withholds
   the client's ledger row, tells the clinician, and lets them settle it.
3. No path through the engine bills a client from a remittance whose two
   statements of their share disagree.
4. make check passes.
notes:
SCOPE CONFIRMED 2026-09-10. This epic owns the whole loop a practice can walk
without anyone else: detect the disagreement, hold the client's bill, tell the
clinician who owns the claim, let them bill it as stated or waive it, and emit
the event naming the remittance behind it.

That is deliberate and not a tier decision. A deployment meeting a
self-contradicting remittance must not silently bill a client the wrong amount,
whoever is running it.

WHAT THIS EPIC DOES NOT OWN: working out WHY the numbers disagreed. Kurt's
call, 2026-09-10 — the investigation, the finding, and turning a real
disagreeing remittance into a committed fixture are the managed tier's job,
not the engine's. The engine's obligation ends at "refuse to guess, tell the
practice, and say which remittance it was". Analysis lives outside it.

So this engine records the hold with enough provenance to FIND the document
again (the transaction it came from, and what our parse believed). It does not
build an evidence corpus. See PABLO-hrak.1, which is being moved off this
board for that reason.

It also makes the loop testable in a browser against the local stack and its
fake clearinghouse, deterministically, instead of only against a deployed
environment — see the e2e child below.

title: Re-emit an open remittance hold every tick, and say so when there are none
description:
A hold is a one-shot event. Crash reports are reliable precisely because
crashes recur: drop one log line and the next request re-emits it. A one-shot
event that is dropped is gone, and whatever was meant to chase it never learns
it existed.

So the emission has to recur until the hold closes, and it has to say "nothing
is open" out loud when nothing is open — because a reader notices a missing
line far sooner than a missing alert.
design:
On an existing scheduled tick, emit one structured log event per OPEN hold,
plus exactly one heartbeat line every run including when the count is zero.

DECISIONS CLOSED:
- Severity is NOTICE/INFO. Never ERROR. A hold is an expected business event;
  raising it to ERROR moves error-rate SLOs and teaches the operator that
  "incident" sometimes means "a customer did an expected thing".
- The event is structured and self-describing: event_type="remittance_hold",
  hold_id, state, age_hours, plus the fields a reader needs to triage. Emitters
  write fields; nothing downstream parses free text.
- The heartbeat is event_type="remittance_hold_heartbeat", open=N, emitted on
  EVERY tick including N=0. Its absence is the signal that the tick, the log
  pipeline, or the environment is dead — which is the only thing that catches
  this whole mechanism rotting during the long quiet before a real payer sends
  an inconsistent remittance.
- Re-emission is per tick per open hold, so a dropped line costs one tick, not
  the hold.
- Where the events GO is per-deployment configuration, not this bead. Emit;
  do not route.
- Guardrail: no PHI in these events. Client identifiers, names and dates of
  service do not appear.

DO NOT build here: any consumer of these events.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A tick with N open holds emits N remittance_hold events, one per hold,
   each carrying hold_id, state and age.
2. A tick with zero open holds still emits exactly one heartbeat line with
   open=0.
3. Every tick emits exactly one heartbeat line — never zero, never two.
4. No event is emitted at ERROR severity.
5. No event carries a client identifier, client name, or date of service; a
   test asserts this against a populated hold.
6. A hold that resolves stops being emitted on the next tick.
7. make check passes.

title: Let a practice settle a held remittance itself
description:
A hold that nobody sees is a client whose balance quietly stops being billed.
The practice needs to meet it as work, and needs to be able to settle it
themselves without waiting for anybody.
design:
Surface an open hold to the clinician who owns the claim, and give them two
resolutions: bill it as stated, or waive it.

DECISIONS CLOSED:
- Both options stay available for the whole life of the hold. They are never
  disabled, never greyed out, and nothing may make the practice wait for an
  answer from anyone in order to act on their own client's balance.
- "Bill as stated" writes the ledger row that was withheld, using the payer's
  stated CLP05, and resolves the hold with finding=bill_as_stated.
- "Waive" resolves with finding=waived and writes no ledger row.
- Both resolutions are audit-logged through the existing audit path.
- app/claims/events.py already carries an unmatched_remittance event kind and
  the machinery for surfacing a claim-level anomaly to a clinician as a
  reminder. EXTEND that; do not invent a parallel notification surface.

DO NOT build here: the hold row itself (sibling bead owns the model and the
posting-path change), the structured event emission (sibling bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A clinician with an open hold sees it as work through the existing claim
   reminder surface, naming the claim and the disagreement.
2. A clinician who does not own the claim does not see it (row policy holds).
3. "Bill as stated" writes exactly the ledger row that was withheld and moves
   the hold to resolved/bill_as_stated.
4. "Waive" moves the hold to resolved/waived and writes no ledger row.
5. Both write an audit entry naming who resolved it and how.
6. Neither option is ever unavailable while the hold is open.
7. make check passes.

title: Hold the client's bill when a remittance contradicts itself
description:
A payer states the client's share of a claim twice in one remittance: once as
a claim total (CLP05) and again itemised across the service lines as PR-group
adjustments. app/claims/remittance_lines.py:146 patient_responsibility_agrees()
already compares them and exempts reversals. It has ZERO production callers —
only tests/test_remittance_lines.py and tests/test_fake_clearinghouse.py. Its
docstring says it "fires on the very first real remittance"; today it fires on
none.

Downstream of that silence, apply_posting (app/claims/remittance.py:277) writes
a row on the client's own ledger. So when the two statements disagree, we bill
a real person an amount our own code cannot corroborate. Over-billing a therapy
client costs trust and is compliance-adjacent; under-billing quietly loses the
practice money. Neither should happen on a number that contradicts itself.
design:
Call patient_responsibility_agrees() from apply_posting BEFORE the ledger
write, and on disagreement record a hold instead of writing the row.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:
- The payer's payment still posts. total_paid_cents, the state advance and the
  "adjudicated" receipt are unaffected. ONLY the charges.add_ledger_row() call
  in the `if charges is not None:` branch is withheld. The check casts doubt on
  the client's share, not on what the payer paid.
- Never auto-release a hold. Time passing is not evidence the number is right.
- A hold is a row with a state and timestamps, not a log line or a flag. States:
  open -> acknowledged -> resolved. Resolution carries a finding:
  bill_as_stated | waived | parse_error | payer_inconsistent.
- The hold is per-tenant. It carries claim id, control number, stated CLP05,
  itemised total, the delta, the CARC/group codes present, line count, payer,
  detected_at.

Model + migration ship together. This is a per-tenant table, so it also needs
its registration wherever this repo registers per-tenant tables, and the tenant
template regenerated.

DO NOT build here: the practice-facing options (sibling bead), the event
emission (sibling bead). This bead ends at "the row exists and the ledger row
was not written".
acceptance_criteria:
1. A remittance whose CLP05 disagrees with its PR itemisation posts the payer's
   payment, advances the claim, writes the adjudicated receipt, and writes NO
   client ledger row.
2. The same remittance leaves exactly one hold row, carrying both totals, the
   delta, the CARC/group codes and the payer.
3. A remittance whose totals agree writes the ledger row exactly as today, and
   leaves no hold. An existing regression test proves the agreeing path is
   unchanged.
4. A reversal (CLP02=22) is exempt and never creates a hold.
5. Re-delivering the same remittance creates no second hold (idempotent on the
   same key the posting path already dedupes on).
6. A fresh tenant provisioned from the template has the hold table.
7. make check passes.

title: Claim findings speak X12 to a therapist: 'subscriber.date_of_birth is required.'
description:
A therapist filing their first claim is told, in red:

  8 things stop this claim from being filed:
  • rendering_provider.last_name is required.
  • rendering_provider.npi is required.
  • subscriber.date_of_birth is required.
  • subscriber.sex is required.
  • subscriber.address_line1 is required.
  • subscriber.city is required.
  • subscriber.state is required.
  • subscriber.postal_code is required.

Every one of those is a field path from the X12 claim, printed verbatim. The
therapist has to know that "rendering_provider" means them, that "subscriber"
means the client (and only because this client is on their own plan — for a
child on a parent's plan it would mean somebody else entirely), and that the
place to fix each one is a different screen.

This is the first thing a new practice sees, because a fresh account trips
every one of these at once. It is the worst-lit moment in the product and it
is on the path to getting paid.

The frame around it is already good — "8 things stop this claim from being
filed", "Worth a look before filing", "What's missing about who files the
claim lives on your practice profile" — so this is not a rewrite of the
review dialog. It is the eight lines inside it.

Captured from a real run: the screenshot is in the e2e artifacts for
frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts, and the setup that satisfies all eight is
givePracticeReadyToBill + giveInsurablePatient in e2e/fixtures/scenarios.ts —
which is a decent inventory of what a practice actually has to have.
design:
WHERE IT COMES FROM. backend/app/claims/superbill.py:

    def _missing(prefix: str, name: str) -> Finding:
        return Finding("blocking", "missing_field",
                       f"{prefix}.{name} is required.", f"{prefix}.{name}")

Finding carries (severity, code, message, field). `field` is the machine
handle and is right as it is — it is what the UI keys on and what a future
"fix this" link will target. `message` is the human sentence and is what is
wrong. Callers: _provider_findings, _patient_findings, _line_findings.

WHAT TO BUILD. A label table, keyed by the SAME (prefix, field) tuple the
finding already carries, giving three things per entry:

  1. what it is, in the practice's words        "Your last name"
  2. whose record it lives on                    practice profile / this
                                                 client's chart / this visit
  3. the sentence                                "Your last name is missing
                                                 from your practice profile."

Then _missing looks the tuple up and uses the sentence. An entry that is
missing falls back to today's text rather than crashing — a new required
field should read badly, not blow up.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate:

* The table lives in the BACKEND, next to superbill.py, not in the frontend.
  The same findings go out through the claim API, the superbill, and the
  biller export; a frontend-only map would fix one of the three.
* `Finding.field` does NOT change. It is the machine handle. Only `message`
  becomes human. The UI already has the handle it needs to build a link.
* "subscriber" is rendered by RELATIONSHIP, not as a fixed word. When
  coverage.subscriber_relationship is "self" the subscriber IS the client and
  the sentence should say "this client"; otherwise it is a different person
  and should say "the subscriber". The claim assembly already knows which
  (assembly.py _subscriber_snapshot branches on exactly this), so the finding
  can be told.
* "rendering_provider" is the signed-in clinician. Say "you" / "your".
* Do not invent new blocking rules, do not change which fields are required,
  and do not touch the scrub's severity split. This is wording.

NICE TO HAVE, in the same PR if it stays small: each finding already knows
which record it belongs to, so the dialog can group the eight into "About you
(2)" and "About this client (6)" and link each group to the screen that fixes
it. The dialog already links to the practice profile, so the pattern exists.

DO NOT TOUCH: the scrub logic, backend/app/claims/assembly.py, the claim
models, anything in the e2e specs beyond an assertion that reads the new copy.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No finding shown to a clinician contains a dotted field path. Grep the rendered copy for '.' between two lowercase words and find nothing.
2. Each of the eight findings in the description reads as a sentence naming what it is and where it lives — e.g. 'Your NPI is missing from your practice profile.' and 'This client's date of birth is missing from their chart.'
3. When the client is the subscriber the copy says so in client terms; when the subscriber is somebody else it says 'the subscriber'. Both covered by a unit test on the finding builder, driven by the two relationship values.
4. Finding.field is unchanged, and a test asserts that — the machine handle is the contract the UI keys on.
5. A field with no entry in the label table still produces a finding, falling back to the current wording, and a test covers that.
6. The same wording reaches the claim API, the superbill and the biller export — one table, three readers, asserted for at least two of them.
7. frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts asserts the new copy in the scrub test instead of the current field path.
notes: Found while writing the first browser test that files a claim (pablo#1056). The screenshot that prompted it is in that PR's e2e artifacts. Sized as one PR; the grouping in NICE TO HAVE is the only part that could reasonably be split off.

title: The clearinghouse's receipts are accepted but never matched, so no claim moves past submitted
description:
Found 2026-09-10 by the first e2e that files a claim in a browser (frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts). A claim is built, scrubbed, filed, and reaches the clearinghouse on the native endpoint. The clearinghouse then posts back the 277CA acknowledgement and the 835 remittance, and the backend answers BOTH with 400 at POST /api/webhooks/clearinghouse. So the claim sits at 'submitted' forever and nothing in the product ever learns it was paid.

The signature verified — a bad signature is 401, and these are 400 — so the payload is being rejected, not the sender. Either the event body the harness posts has drifted from what the handler parses, or the handler's schema is wrong about the real shape. 23 unit tests cover this handler and every one of them passes, which is the point: they were all written against a body we authored.

Observed in the compose stack: fake webhook log shows kind=277 status=400 and kind=835 status=400, backend access log shows POST /api/webhooks/clearinghouse -> 400 twice.
design:
Read backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/webhook_transaction_processed.json — it is a CONSTRUCTED fixture, per the fixtures README, so it is not evidence of the real shape. Get the actual rejected body out of the harness first (scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py _deliver builds it), diff it against what the handler validates, and decide which side is wrong against the vendor's documented event schema rather than against either of our own artefacts.

Then extend frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts back to 'paid': the spec deliberately stops at the clearinghouse today and says so in its header, and the assertion that belongs there is already written in the git history of this bead's branch.

DO NOT weaken the signature check or the 400-vs-401 split to make this pass (guardrail S4).
acceptance_criteria:
1. POST /api/webhooks/clearinghouse accepts the 277CA the harness posts and returns 2xx.
2. The same for the 835.
3. A claim filed in the compose stack reaches state 'paid' with total_paid_cents set.
4. frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts asserts 'paid' rather than 'submitted', and its header no longer says it stops early.
5. Whichever side was wrong is corrected against the vendor's documented event schema, and the reasoning is in the commit message.
notes:
PARTLY FIXED 2026-09-10 on branch enrollment-tasks (pablo#1056).

The 400 is gone. Cause: the harness posted an EventBridge-shaped envelope
(source / detail-type / detail, transaction document inline) and the reader
wants the vendor's own event envelope (id / type / resource naming the
transaction, object: v1.event). parse_event found no 'type', returned None,
and the route answered 400 'expected an event object'.

Both shapes were CONSTRUCTED — neither is a capture — so the tie was broken by
webhook_transaction_processed.json, which is what the reader and its 23 tests
were written against, and which carries the vendor envelope. The harness now
posts that. Verified: both deliveries return 200.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is the reason this bead stays open. The receipts are now
accepted and then go nowhere:

  clearinghouse_webhook_processed event=... transaction=... outcome=unmatched   (277CA)
  clearinghouse_webhook_processed event=... transaction=... outcome=ignored     (835)

So ingest_transaction_event fetches the transaction and fails to tie it to the
claim, and the claim stays 'submitted' with total_paid_cents 0. That matching
step is the next thing to read. Start at whatever ingest_transaction_event
matches on (control number, most likely) and compare it against what the
harness puts in the transaction document for a claim submitted through the
NATIVE endpoint — the document is built by _legacy_shape_for_reports, which is
a conversion, and a conversion is exactly where a control number goes missing.

THE REAL LESSON, worth keeping: this whole class of bug exists because both
sides of the seam were authored. The first genuinely captured event will
settle the envelope question for good — see the dev webhook lane (PABLO-1lem);
when a real destination is enabled, capture the first event.ping and the first
transaction.processed and replace the constructed fixture with them.
2026-09-10, pablo#1068 (tests only, no fix yet).

Mutation-tested the existing coverage before touching anything. The 25 unit
tests in tests/test_claim_webhooks.py all stub tenant_db_session and both
repositories, and hand PracticeContext a hardcoded user_ids list. Result:

  practice_user_ids returns []   -> unit suite 31 PASSED, blind
  matching can never find a claim -> only 2 of 31 fail

So the step that decides WHO IS ASKED whether they can see the claim was
exercised by nothing, and 'unmatched' is exactly what an empty or wrong
user list produces. That is the leading hypothesis for the observed
symptom: the document shapes are fine (the unit fake is built from the
CAPTURED fixtures, so those are faithful), and the visibility fan-out is
the part no test crossed.

Also noted: test_a_transaction_naming_no_claim_of_ours_is_unmatched passes
under EVERY mutation, including matching disabled entirely. It asserts the
failure outcome, so it cannot tell correct-unmatched from broken-matching.

pablo#1068 adds four tests that run the fan-out against real tenant
sessions, the real platform registry, the real email-to-practice map and
the real row policy, with only the vendor faked. Three of the four fail
against the empty-list mutation.

STILL OPEN — this bead does not close on #1068:
  - The actual root cause is not yet confirmed against the compose run.
    Next step is still the bead's original design note: reproduce with
    docker-compose.e2e.yml and read what get_transaction actually returns
    for the 835, and which user ids the loop walks.
  - Two early-return defects found by reading, not yet fixed and not yet
    reproduced (they need two practices sharing one clearinghouse account):
    fanout.py returns 'unmatched' as soon as ONE practice fetches an ack it
    cannot match instead of trying the rest, and the same early return
    applies to 'ignored' on the remittance branch.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-10, reproduced in docker-compose.e2e.yml. It is not a
matching failure and never was.

THE CLIENT AND THE HARNESS DISAGREE ABOUT THE REPORT URL.

  app/claims/stedi.py:422 / :437 fetch reports at
    /2024-04-01/change/medicalnetwork/reports/v2/{transaction_id}/{277|835}
  scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py serves reports ONLY at
    /2023-08-01/transactions/{transaction_id}/{input|output}   (line 774)

Proved by hand against the running harness, for the transaction the webhook
actually named:

  200  /2023-08-01/transactions/<tx>            (1712 bytes)
  200  /2023-08-01/transactions/<tx>/output     (2229 bytes)
  200  /2023-08-01/transactions/<tx>/input      (2229 bytes)
  404  /2024-04-01/change/medicalnetwork/reports/v2/<tx>/835
  404  /2024-04-01/change/medicalnetwork/reports/v2/<tx>/277

WHAT EACH DELIVERY THEN DOES, and why they look different:

277CA -> the report 404s -> ClearinghouseNotFoundError -> caught by
  fanout.py's `except ClearinghouseNotFoundError: continue` -> the practice
  loop exhausts -> ingest_transaction_event returns its initial value,
  "unmatched", with HTTP 200. THE "unmatched" IN THE ORIGINAL REPORT WAS THIS,
  not a control-number mismatch. Observed: outcome=unmatched, HTTP 200.

835 -> the same 404, but fetch_remittance is called OUTSIDE that try block
  (fanout.py:162), so the error escapes the route: HTTP 500 with
  ClearinghouseNotFoundError. Observed.

SO THERE ARE TWO DEFECTS, and only one of them is the harness:

(1) TEST INFRASTRUCTURE. The harness does not serve the report path the client
    uses. Same family as PABLO-ukzm. Fixing this alone would make the e2e go
    green and would leave (2) in the product.

(2) PRODUCT, and the more serious one. fanout.py treats
    ClearinghouseNotFoundError as "some other account owns this transaction,
    try the next practice" — which is what the docstring says it means. But the
    same exception is raised when the report endpoint is wrong, unreachable, or
    the vendor has changed it. So a genuine integration failure is silently
    reported as "unmatched", indistinguishable from "no claim of ours", and
    nothing alerts. Meanwhile the remittance branch is not protected at all and
    answers 500.

    The 500 matters more than it looks now that the dev event destination is
    ENABLED (2026-09-10): the vendor retries failed deliveries, and repeated
    failures can get a destination disabled at the vendor end — the exact
    hazard docs/internal/clearinghouse-stedi-setup.md warns about when it says
    to enable a destination only after its mount ships.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S EARLIER NOTE: the leading hypothesis recorded earlier
today was RLS / practice_user_ids visibility. That is DISPROVEN as the cause
here — the fan-out never got as far as asking anybody, because the report fetch
404'd first. The integration tests added in pablo#1068 remain worth having (the
fan-out genuinely had no coverage, and practice_user_ids returning [] still
leaves the unit suite green), but they did not find this and were not what was
wrong.

NEXT: fix (2) first — distinguish "this account does not own it" from "we could
not read the report", stop the remittance branch escaping as a 500, and make an
integration failure loud rather than "unmatched". Then (1) so the e2e can reach
paid, which is PABLO-d8ow.17.
CORRECTION 2026-09-10, recorded because an earlier note here overstated it.

I wrote that the unguarded ClearinghouseNotFoundError meant "a real
transaction.processed arriving at dev would 500", and that claim was used to
justify re-parking the dev event destination. It is not right.

Measured against DEPLOYED dev (then on 1f96092f, i.e. BEFORE pablo#1073), with
a synthetic but correctly-signed transaction.processed naming REAL inbound
transactions in the vendor's test account:

  real INBOUND 277 (8c73c3c5…) -> HTTP 200 {"outcome":"unmatched"}
  real INBOUND 835 (d19a0d9b…) -> HTTP 200 {"outcome":"unmatched"}

No 500. The reason is that the 500 needed the REPORT FETCH to 404, and that
was the fake clearinghouse's doing — it served no such path. Against the real
vendor the report paths are correct and the fetch succeeds.

The outcome proves it rather than assuming: under the pre-fix code a document
that is not a remittance returns "ignored". These returned "unmatched", which
is only reachable after fetch_remittance returned a PARSED remittance — so
production code fetched and parsed a real 835 report from the real vendor.
That is independent confirmation that the adapter's paths were right and the
harness was the thing that was wrong.

The 500 remains a real hazard, just an unobserved one: it needs a 404 from the
vendor — a report not yet materialised when the event fires, a changed path, a
permission on the report but not on the transaction. pablo#1073 turns all of
those into a 503 and a loud log instead of an unhandled exception, which is
still worth having. But "dev would 500 on a real delivery" was wrong, and
anyone reading this bead should not repeat it.

title: A therapist cannot complete enrollment paperwork in Pablo, though the vendor API allows it
description: When a payer wants a form signed or a document uploaded, we surface the vendor's instructions and a link. The therapist leaves Pablo to finish it, and Pablo never learns whether they did except by polling. There is no document upload path and no handling of the vendor's enrollment events.
design:
CORRECTED 2026-09-10 after reading the vendor docs properly. An earlier
version of this bead hedged that the vendor "may not expose an upload
endpoint". It does, and the whole task-completion workflow is API-driven. A
therapist can finish enrollment paperwork inside Pablo; today they cannot,
and that is the gap.

WHAT THE VENDOR ACTUALLY OFFERS. Fourteen enrollment endpoints. Our adapter
implements THREE:
  implemented : post-enrollment-create-provider, post-enrollment-create-
                enrollment, get-enrollment-list-enrollments
  missing     : get-enrollment (retrieve one, with task and document detail),
                post-enrollment-update-task, post-enrollment-document-upload,
                get-enrollment-document-download, delete-enrollment-document,
                post-enrollment-update-enrollment, delete-enrollment,
                get-enrollment-list-providers, get-enrollment-provider,
                post-enrollment-update-provider, delete-enrollment-provider

A TASK IS A FORM, NOT A NOTE. `definition.manualTask` carries `fields[]`,
each with `key`, `label`, `description` and `fieldType` — allowed values
`TEXT` and `DOCUMENT`. Our `EnrollmentManualTask` model has only
`instructions` and `links`, so we read the prose and drop the machine-
actionable half entirely. That is why it looks like a link-out: we made it
one.

THE DOCUMENT WORKFLOW, exactly:
 1. GET the enrollment to read the task, its fields, and any document status.
 2. POST /enrollments/{enrollmentId}/documents with {name, taskId}. Returns
    `uploadUrl` (a pre-signed S3 URL, expires in 24h) and `documentId`.
 3. PUT the bytes to `uploadUrl` with `Content-Type: application/pdf`.
    PDF only. NOTE: this PUT goes to AWS, not to the vendor — it does not
    carry the vendor API key and it does NOT go through
    `ClearinghouseCredentials.base_url`. The e2e fake will need to stand in
    for an S3 URL it hands out itself, or the adapter needs a seam for it.
 4. Poll GET enrollment until the document status moves PENDING -> UPLOADED
    (usually under 10 seconds; FAILED is a real outcome and must be shown).
 5. POST update-task with `values[]`, one object per field: the field `key`
    plus a `value` carrying either the text or `{document: {documentId}}`.
    Only then is the task complete.

BUILD, in this order:
 * Model: give `EnrollmentTask` its id, and `EnrollmentManualTask` its
   `fields[]`; add the document status shape. Capture fixtures from the
   recorded enrollment rather than hand-building — the account already has a
   real enrollment (see the fixtures README).
 * Protocol + adapter: `get_enrollment`, `upload_enrollment_document`,
   `update_enrollment_task`, and the raw PUT as its own small seam so it can
   be faked.
 * Routes + UI: render an open PROVIDER task as a form — text inputs for
   TEXT fields, a PDF picker for DOCUMENT fields, the vendor's instructions
   and template link above it. On submit: upload, poll, complete, refresh.
 * The compliance reminder keeps pointing at that form rather than at the
   vendor.

WHAT THESE DOCUMENTS ARE: practice paperwork — signed enrollment forms, W-9s,
provider agreements. Not patient data, so this is not a PHI surface. They do
carry the practice's tax id and a signature, so treat them as sensitive
practice records: never logged, never in an error message, and the download
URL is short-lived by the vendor's design.

ENROLLMENT EVENTS, still true and still worth doing: the vendor publishes
`enrollment.activated`, `enrollment.task.assigned` and `enrollment.document`,
and our destinations subscribe to `transaction.processed` and `event.ping`
only. `enrollment.task.assigned` is the moment the payer asks the therapist
for something. Add the subscription only once a handler exists — the webhook
acknowledges and ignores unknown types, so subscribing early just makes
delivery volume that does nothing. Destinations: dev
`dst_01a08967-20e0-76e3-a47f-e59bb41b61eb`, prod
`dst_01a0896e-4d1c-7783-8055-d17f2b5ebbfd`.

ORDER: PABLO-5zlm first (the status poll is not scheduled at all, so nothing
in this area updates today), then this.

OUT OF SCOPE: credentialing. Becoming in-network is a months-long process
between the therapist and the payer, upstream of EDI enrollment entirely.

THE TESTING CONSTRAINT, probed directly 2026-09-10 — read this before
estimating.

A test key reaches almost everything. Measured, not assumed:
    claims list / submit / timeline .... 200
    payer search ....................... 200
    transactions feed .................. 200
    event destinations ................. works (two created this way)
    ENROLLMENT, all 14 endpoints ....... 403

The vendor states it plainly: "You must complete the enrollment in production
- you can't submit enrollments with a test API key or in test mode."

So this bead cannot be exercised the way the claims work was. There is no test
lane for it at all.

AND THE ONE CHEAP REAL ENROLLMENT DOES NOT HELP. Enrolling with the vendor's
own Test Payer (production key, production mode) is documented and is how this
account got set up - but the vendor "automatically sets the enrollment request
to LIVE status within one minute". It goes create-provider -> create-enrollment
-> LIVE and NEVER assigns a task, requests a document, or reaches
PROVIDER_ACTION_REQUIRED. Which is exactly the half this bead is about.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR HOW TO BUILD IT:
* The only PROVIDER_ACTION_REQUIRED artefact we hold
  (`enrollment_provider_action_required.json`) is CONSTRUCTED, not captured -
  the fixtures README says so, and says why: a test key can never produce it.
  So the task and document code would be written against a shape we invented.
* The first honest validation is a real enrollment, for a real practice, with
  a real payer, in production.

RECOMMENDATION: build this ALONGSIDE the first customer's enrollment rather
than ahead of it, with somebody watching the vendor's portal in parallel and
capturing what actually arrives. Ship the read-only half first (show the task,
its fields and its links, faithfully) so a therapist can at least see what is
being asked while the completion path is written against real shapes. Do not
let a constructed fixture become the definition of done here - that is the
mistake pablo#1038 already cost us once, on a smaller number.

FULL SPEC IN HAND, 2026-09-10 — this supersedes the "build it alongside the
first customer" caution above. Two different things were conflated there: we
cannot VERIFY against a real payer task without production, but we can CONFORM
to the API exactly, because the vendor documents it completely with worked
examples. Build it now; let the first real enrollment confirm it.

Source: https://www.stedi.com/docs/healthcare/transaction-enrollment-tasks-documents

FOUR TASK SHAPES, not two. Read `definition.manualTask.fields[]`:
  * EMPTY fields[]  - follow the instructions somewhere else (a payer portal,
    a phone call). Complete with `{"completed": true}` and nothing else.
  * TEXT fields     - collect strings.
  * DOCUMENT fields - upload a PDF.
  * MIXED           - both in one task. Submit every value together.
A task with fields REQUIRES a value for every field to complete.

THE COMPLETION ENDPOINT IS ON THE TASK, NOT THE ENROLLMENT:
  POST https://enrollments.us.stedi.com/2024-09-01/tasks/{taskId}
  {"completed": true, "responseData": {"manualTask": {"values": [
      {"key": "MEDICAID_ID",     "value": {"text": "ABCD12"}},
      {"key": "ENROLLMENT_FORM", "value": {"document": {"documentId": "..."}}}
  ]}}}
Field keys are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and come from the task definition.

TASK FIELDS WE DO NOT MODEL AND NEED: `id` (required to complete it),
`isComplete`, `rank` (display order), and `definition.manualTask.fields[]`
with `key` / `label` / `description` / `fieldType`.

LINKS ARE TWO KINDS AND MUST BE TOLD APART:
  * starting `https://enrollments.us.stedi.com/` - a Stedi document. An
    AUTHENTICATED GET returns a pre-signed `downloadUrl` (24h); a second
    unauthenticated GET fetches the PDF. Two hops.
  * anything else - an external resource, link out as-is.
Rendering a Stedi URL as a plain href gives the therapist a 401.

UPLOAD, unchanged from above: POST /enrollments/{id}/documents {name, taskId}
-> {uploadUrl, documentId}; PUT the bytes to uploadUrl with
Content-Type: application/pdf (PDF only); poll until the document is UPLOADED
(FAILED is real); then complete the task quoting documentId.

POLLING IS ALREADY SUPPORTED BY OUR CLIENT. The vendor recommends listing
enrollments filtered to PROVIDER_ACTION_REQUIRED and checking `tasks[]` for
`isComplete: false`. `EnrollmentFilters.statuses` already exists and maps to
the `status` query parameter, so this needs no new adapter surface — only the
richer task model.

THE THERAPIST IS ALREADY BEING EMAILED, which shrinks the notification gap
recorded on PABLO-oaxi: "the email address listed as the Stedi contact person
receives a notification that there is a new task to complete", and
`_request()` already sends `userEmail=contact.email` from the practice
billing profile. So the payer-is-waiting signal DOES reach a human today. What
is missing is the in-app surface and any way to act on it — not the alert.

AND COMPLETING A TASK NEEDS NO EXTRA POKE: "Stedi is automatically notified
when you complete a task, and the enrollment process continues."

TEST MODE STILL REFUSES IT — checked directly 2026-09-10, after a suggestion
that it might have opened up. A POST to /providers with the test key answers:

    HTTP 403
    {"code":"access_denied",
     "message":"Access Denied - This functionality is not available in Test Mode."}

The vendor's own words, not an inference. The docs were also re-fetched and are
byte-identical to yesterday's copy. So enrollment remains production-only.

WHAT WE COULD CHECK INSTEAD, and did: read the REAL production provider record
and enrollment (read-only, with the production key). Both parse against our
models, and two shapes are worth writing down because they were captured, not
assumed:

  provider record ....... id, name, npi, taxId, taxIdType
      NOTE: the response carries NO `contacts` key, even though the request
      sends contacts. `ProviderRecord.contacts` defaults to [], which is why
      this has never failed — but do not rely on reading a contact back.

  enrollment ............ aggregationPreference, createdAt, documents,
                          history, id, payer, provider, requestedEffectiveDate,
                          source, status, statusLastUpdatedAt, submittedAt,
                          transactions, updatedAt
      status LIVE, transactions {claimPayment} — the Test Payer 835
      enrollment this account was set up with.

TWO FIELDS WE DO NOT MODEL AND SHOULD, both confirmed present on a real record:
  * `documents` — top level on the enrollment. This is where uploaded PDFs
    live, so it is the read side of this bead. Model it alongside `tasks`.
  * `history` — the status trail. Probably how "what changed and when" should
    be shown to a therapist rather than us reconstructing it from polls.

`tasks` and `reason` are simply absent on a LIVE enrollment with nothing
outstanding, which is consistent with them being situational — not evidence
that our modelling of them is wrong, and not evidence that it is right.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The task model carries its id and its fields, with fieldType TEXT and DOCUMENT distinguished.
2. A PROVIDER task renders as a form: the vendor instructions, its template link, a text input per TEXT field and a PDF picker per DOCUMENT field.
3. Uploading a PDF gets a pre-signed URL, PUTs the bytes, and waits for the document to reach UPLOADED before completing the task; a FAILED document is shown, not swallowed.
4. Completing the task posts one value per field and the enrollment reflects it without waiting for the daily poll.
5. A therapist can finish an enrollment task without leaving Pablo or holding a clearinghouse login.
6. Documents are never logged and never appear in an error message.
7. make check passes.
notes:
worker alive (runtime poll) — heartbeat
worker exited with PR (open) — office poll tagged pr-open

TWO PRs FOR THIS BEAD, built in parallel 2026-09-10. Pick one as trunk and
port the other's strengths; do not merge both.

  #1055 work/therapist-enrollment-fix (fleet). CI green. 20 unit tests
        including adapter-level ones on stedi.py. Has a link-resolution
        endpoint that turns a vendor-hosted template link into a presigned
        download and refuses to resolve external links. No e2e, no fake
        clearinghouse support.

  #1056 enrollment-tasks (interactive session). Same three routes and the
        same form, plus: the fake clearinghouse grows the document
        lifecycle (slot -> bytes -> completion, refusing a completion
        naming a document whose bytes never arrived), a download URL base
        separate from the upload base because one is followed by the server
        and the other by the browser, and two Playwright specs that drive
        upload and read-back against the compose stack and assert the
        ORDER of what the clearinghouse received. Merged with main.

  Recommendation: #1056 as trunk (it satisfies the e2e half of the ask and
  the ordering is what this feature is actually about), then port #1055's
  adapter tests and its task-link resolution.
PR closed unmerged — reconciled
close_reason:
Merged in pablo#1056 (4d1cd8bd). A therapist can now answer an enrollment task in Pablo: read it as a form, type what it asks for, upload the signed PDF, and open the payer's blank form — which needs the account key, so it is fetched through us rather than linked at a 403.

Built as the bead asked: models gained the task fields and document statuses; the protocol and adapter gained get_enrollment, upload_enrollment_document, put_document (its own seam, because the bytes go to the vendor's object store with no API key), download_enrollment_document, resolve_enrollment_link and complete_enrollment_task; routes and UI render an open PROVIDER task as a form.

The ordering the bead spelled out is enforced and TESTED: ask for a slot, write the bytes, wait for UPLOADED, only then complete. A task is never completed against a document that is still PENDING, and a FAILED one raises rather than completing.

Not covered, and still true: the bead's warning that the only PROVIDER_ACTION_REQUIRED artefact we hold is CONSTRUCTED. Nothing here has been seen against a real payer, and the recommendation to validate alongside the first customer's real enrollment stands. The e2e harness is the substitute, not the proof.

Out of scope as the bead said: credentialing. Enrollment events (enrollment.task.assigned) not subscribed — that waits on a handler, and on the dev webhook lane (PABLO-1lem).

title: Give the practice a way to refresh enrollment status at all
description: Enrollment requests are filed automatically when a payer is added, and a daily job exists to poll their status — but that job is not scheduled in dev or prod. So a request is submitted and then never updates, and the one state that needs a human never surfaces.
design:
RESHAPED 2026-09-10. The first version of this bead said "schedule the job".
That is still wanted, but it is the second step, not the first: a button gets
the practice unstuck tonight with no infrastructure at all, and the function
is already built for it.

WHAT EXISTS. `refresh_enrollments(session, client, *, limit, arm, now)` in
`backend/app/claims/enrollment.py` takes a session and a client, does ONE
listing per pass narrowed to this practice's provider and the payers with open
requests, reads at most `MAX_LIST_PAGES`, matches at most `limit` requests,
records what changed, mirrors each payer's overall status, raises
`enrollment_action_required`, and DOES NOT COMMIT — the caller owns the
transaction. That is a route's shape, not a job's. `sync_provider_record`
already calls into this module from a route the same way
(`backend/app/routes/practice_billing.py`).

WHAT IS MISSING is only the entry point. The payer routes today file
(`POST /api/payers/{id}/enrollments`) and list (`GET` the same), and nothing
refreshes.

BUILD:
 * `POST /api/payers/enrollments/refresh` — practice-scoped, no payer id: one
   listing covers every open request the practice has, so refreshing per payer
   would make N vendor calls to answer one question. Returns how many changed
   so the button can say something true ("nothing has moved yet" is a useful
   answer).
 * A refresh control on the payers / billing surface, showing when it last ran
   and what changed.
 * Rate-limit it per practice. The vendor moves in days; a therapist clicking
   twice a second must not become two vendor calls a second. A short floor
   (a minute) and returning the previous answer inside it is enough.
 * No clearinghouse configured is the existing 503 shape, not a crash.

WHY A BUTTON IS GENUINELY ENOUGH TO START: today NOTHING updates, ever. A
practice that files an enrollment sees its initial status forever. A button
takes that from "impossible" to "whenever anyone looks", which is most of the
value for a first customer who is watching the screen because they are waiting.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SOLVE, and this is the real argument for the job that follows:
the state that matters most is `PROVIDER_ACTION_REQUIRED` — the payer asking
the THERAPIST for something. Nobody is refreshing a page to discover they have
homework. And the compliance reminder is generated BY the refresh, so with no
poll the reminder never fires, which means the notification path never fires
either. The button makes the data right when looked at; only the job makes
somebody find out without looking.

DO NOT refresh on page load without a throttle: it puts a vendor call in the
render path of a page people open all day.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A practice-scoped refresh endpoint polls every open enrollment in one listing and reports how many changed.
2. A control on the billing surface calls it and shows what changed, including "nothing moved".
3. Repeated presses inside the throttle window return the previous answer without a second vendor call.
4. A request that moves to PROVIDER_ACTION_REQUIRED raises the event and produces the compliance reminder with the vendor instructions.
5. A practice with no clearinghouse gets the existing 503 shape.
6. make check + frontend gates green.
notes:
worker exited with PR (open) — office poll tagged pr-open
PR merged (https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/1053) — reconciled

title: Prove the clearinghouse webhook against dev with real vendor events
description: The webhook path has 23 unit tests and has never received a real vendor event, because no event destination exists on the account. The local stack cannot close this: the vendor cannot post to a laptop. Only a publicly reachable deployment can.
design:
FOUND 2026-09-09: `list_event_destinations` on the account returns ZERO. The
vendor is posting webhooks nowhere, so the whole path — signature
verification, `app/claims/fanout.py`, the 277CA application — has never run
against a real delivery in any environment. Acknowledgements currently reach
claims through the pipeline's polling stage instead, so nothing is broken;
the webhook is simply unproven and unused.

`CLEARINGHOUSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set ONLY in `docker-compose.e2e.yml`. No
deployment sets it.

TWO PREREQUISITES, BOTH KURT'S TO AUTHORISE — do not perform them from a
coding session:
  P1. Create an event destination on the Stedi account pointing at
      `https://dev.pablo.health/api/webhooks/clearinghouse`, subscribed to
      `transaction.processed`. This is an outward-facing change: it tells a
      vendor to start sending traffic to our deployment.
  P2. Put that destination's secret in dev's Secret Manager and wire it to
      `CLEARINGHOUSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. The setting already supports rotation
      via `clearinghouse_webhook_secret_previous`, so use that when rotating
      rather than swapping in place.

THEN BUILD a lane at `backend/tests_integration/dev_webhook/`, modelled on
`clearinghouse_live/` — opt-in, skipped without credentials, never run in the
ordinary PR job:

1. Authenticate to dev as the pinned end-to-end account.
2. Seed a client, coverage against the vendor TEST payer, and a session with
   codes. Synthetic data only, the vendor's documented example person.
3. File the claim through dev's own API.
4. Wait for the acknowledgement to appear on the claim.

THE ASSERTION THAT MAKES THIS WORTH HAVING: prove the WEBHOOK applied it, not
the poller. Both produce an acknowledged claim, so a test that only checks
"the claim was acknowledged" proves nothing the polling lane does not already
prove. Two discriminators, use both:
  * TIME. The webhook arrives within seconds; the pipeline runs on
    `CLAIMS_PIPELINE_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 5). Assert the receipt lands
    well inside a minute.
  * PROVENANCE. A webhook-applied receipt carries the vendor's EVENT id as
    its `vendor_event_id` (see `fanout.py::_apply_in_practice`, which passes
    `event_id`), where a polled one does not. Assert the shape.

DECISIONS CLOSED:
* This lane writes real rows into dev. That is acceptable and is why it uses
  the pinned test account and synthetic data; it is not acceptable to point
  it at production.
* Scheduled or manual only. It depends on the vendor, the network and a
  deployment being up, so it must never gate a pull request.
* Do NOT disable the pipeline on dev to force the webhook to be the only
  path. Leave both running and discriminate on provenance — that is closer to
  what production does anyway.

WORTH DECIDING SEPARATELY, and noted here so it is not lost: the webhook
currently ignores anything that is not a 277CA
(`test_a_document_that_is_not_a_277_is_ignored` pins that as intended), so an
835 still waits for the timer. Teaching it to post an 835 is PABLO-4emu.

PREREQUISITE P1 IS DONE, 2026-09-09, authorised by Kurt in session.

  destination id : dst_01a08967-20e0-76e3-a47f-e59bb41b61eb
  url            : https://dev.pablo.health/api/webhooks/clearinghouse
  event types    : transaction.processed, event.ping
  mode           : TEST (created with the test-mode key)
  status         : DISABLED  <- deliberately parked, see below
  secret         : whsec_-prefixed, 50 chars, written 0600 to the session
                   scratchpad. NOT in this repo and not in any transcript.
                   Re-read it any time with GetEventDestinationSecret on the
                   destination id above.

WHY TEST MODE MATTERS, and it is the thing that makes this safe: the vendor
documents that "event destinations you create in test mode only receive test
events". Production claims therefore never reach dev, so no production PHI
can arrive in a dev environment through this path. A destination created with
a PRODUCTION-mode key is a separate object and is what production will need -
see below.

WHY IT IS PARKED DISABLED: dev has no `CLEARINGHOUSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (it is
set only in docker-compose.e2e.yml today), so every delivery would 401. The
vendor retries, emails the account about repeated failures, and can disable a
destination itself. Enabling is one call once the secret is wired.

REMAINING, and these need GCP rights this session does not have (the signed-in
account has no run/secretmanager permission on pablohealth-prod):
  1. Put the secret in Secret Manager for dev.
  2. Wire it to `CLEARINGHOUSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` on the dev backend service and
     deploy. `clearinghouse_webhook_secret_previous` already exists in
     settings for rotation - use it rather than swapping in place.
  3. Re-enable the destination (UpdateEventDestination, status ENABLED).
  4. Then the lane below can be written.

PRODUCTION WILL NEED ITS OWN, and it is a different object, not a promotion of
this one: create a destination with a PRODUCTION-mode key pointing at
https://app.pablo.health/api/webhooks/clearinghouse, with its own secret in
the prod project. Until that exists, production acknowledgements arrive only
through the pipeline poller - which works, but means a practice waits up to
CLAIMS_PIPELINE_INTERVAL_MINUTES to see a payer response.

WORTH ADDING WHILE BUILDING THE LANE: the event payload carries
`environment: TEST | PRODUCTION`. Dev should refuse a PRODUCTION event outright
rather than trusting the mode of the key that fetched it - cheap
defence-in-depth against a misconfigured destination ever pointing the wrong
environment at the wrong deployment.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The lane skips cleanly with no credentials and never runs in the ordinary PR job.
2. It files a claim through dev and observes the acknowledgement land.
3. It asserts the acknowledgement arrived within a minute — far inside the pipeline interval.
4. It asserts the receipt carries the vendor event id, proving the webhook applied it rather than the poller.
5. Only synthetic data reaches dev, and nothing points at production.
6. A run is recorded on the bead, since this is the first real vendor delivery the code has ever seen.

title: The e2e harness cannot produce a partial payment, or post an 835 promptly
description: A billing end-to-end spec cannot be written against the harness as it stands: the fake clearinghouse only ever pays in full, and the 835 reaches a claim only on the pipeline's five-minute timer.
design:
Found by running the suite on 2026-09-09. The lane is healthy - 33 specs pass
in about 30 seconds - but two gaps block any spec about money, and both are
worth fixing on their own merits.

A. THE FAKE ONLY PAYS IN FULL. `scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py`
   `_build_835_report` substitutes the claim's own amounts into
   `835_report_paid_in_full.json` and pays all of it, so patient
   responsibility is never anything but zero. Add control-number rules beside
   the existing `REJ-DX` / `REJ-PTR` / `REJ-SUB` ones:
   * `PART-` -> pays part, assigns the remainder as PR on the service line
     (CAS group PR), CLP05 set to match the sum of PR - the parser now checks
     that agreement, so an inconsistent fake would be caught by our own code.
   * `DENY-` -> a denial that leaves the client owing the charge.
   Derive both from the recorded 835 rather than hand-building a new one.

B. AN 835 WAITS UP TO FIVE MINUTES. The clearinghouse webhook handles 277CA
   acknowledgements only (`app/claims/fanout.py`: "an inbound document that is
   not a 277CA is ignored"); the 835 is posted by the pipeline remit stage on
   `CLAIMS_PIPELINE_INTERVAL_MINUTES`, default 5, and nothing sets it in
   `docker-compose.e2e.yml`.

   This is a product latency bug as much as a test one: a practice waits up to
   five minutes after a payer pays before the app says so, even though the
   vendor told us immediately. Teach the webhook to post an 835 the way it
   posts a 277CA - fan out to the owning practice, read the claim's timeline,
   post through the existing `apply_posting`, which is already idempotent on
   the vendor entry id so the timer re-running afterwards is harmless.

   Do NOT shorten the timer as the fix. That leaves the latency in production
   and makes the suite slow.

C. NOT IN SCOPE: a Stripe fake. Card charges cannot be driven from a browser
   today and the self-pay half of a balance therefore cannot be tested end to
   end. Say so in the notes; do not add one here.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A claim whose control number begins `PART-` comes back part paid with the remainder assigned as patient responsibility, and its CLP05 agrees with the sum of its PR adjustments.
2. A claim whose control number begins `DENY-` comes back denied with the client owing the charge.
3. An 835 delivered by webhook posts the remittance immediately; a test proves the claim reads paid without waiting for the pipeline timer.
4. The pipeline timer re-running afterwards posts nothing a second time.
5. `make check` passes and the existing e2e lane stays green.

title: Get real payer ERAs from a design partner
description: No public artifact validates remittance semantics against real payer behaviour. Real ERAs from a working therapist do, and are obtainable now rather than at first customer.
design:
The clearinghouse test payer pays every claim in full and emits no
adjustments, so nothing in the suite has ever seen a contractual write-off, a
deductible, a denial or a secondary claim from a real payer.

Standards bodies do not close this. X12 TR3 examples are licensed and cannot be
committed to a public repo; CAQH CORE certification decks live with the
authorised testing vendor; state Medicaid sample files are claim-level denials
with no service-line detail. Open-source 835 samples are hand-made too.

What does close it: a single solo therapist on Office Ally or Availity can
download their raw 835 files and hand over months of real Aetna / BCBS / UHC /
Cigna / Optum / Medicare ERAs - the exact payer mix our customers bring. Costs
a BAA and a conversation.

Needs a BAA before any file changes hands, and the files are PHI: they are
evidence to read and to derive scrubbed fixtures from, NOT artifacts to commit.
Scrub to the vendor-example-person pattern the existing fixtures use.

Free and worth reading while arranging this: X12 RFI 2601 (allowed vs charge vs
PR45), RFI 2535 (secondary OA23), RFI 1705 (interest); CMS Claims Processing
Manual chapter 22 (public domain, authoritative on CO/PR/OA and sequestration);
the CAQH CORE Rule 360 code-combination table.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A BAA is in place with the design partner before any ERA changes hands.
2. Real ERAs covering at least a contractual write-off, a deductible and a denial have been read.
3. Scrubbed fixtures derived from them are committed; no raw partner file is.
4. Each quarantine shape the ERAs prove out is relaxed, or recorded as still unproven.
notes:
SETTLED BY QUERY 2026-09-10, not by reading docs. Kurt pushed on whether the
vendor really has no test-mode lever for a denial or a partial payment, on the
grounds that the claim rested on documentation — and documentation had already
been wrong twice today. So the payer network was asked directly with our own
test key.

    payer search "test"  -> FRCPB  "Stedi Test Payer"   (ONE result)
    payer search "mock"  -> nothing
    payer search "demo"  -> real payers whose NAMES contain "demo"
                            (Caresource Military and Veterans, TRISTAR
                            Insurance Group), not fixtures

THERE IS EXACTLY ONE TEST PAYER. No denial variant, no partial-payment
variant, no second mock to point a claim at. Its declared support:

    professionalClaimSubmission  SUPPORTED
    eligibilityCheck             SUPPORTED
    claimPayment                 ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED
    coordinationOfBenefits       NOT_SUPPORTED

So what test mode CAN and CANNOT produce, with the evidence for each:

  claim REJECTION      YES. "Stedi doesn't forward test claims to payers.
                       Instead, we apply our entire catalog of edits and
                       repairs and then generate a test 277CA claim
                       acknowledgment indicating whether the test claim passed
                       our validation." Proven by our own three captured
                       837p_submission_edit_rejected_* fixtures, which were
                       made by submitting genuinely invalid claims.

  eligibility failures YES. Documented mock members; we hold captures of
                       inactive coverage and of an AAA error.

  DENIAL (CLP02=4)     NO lever found.
  PARTIAL / CO-45      NO lever found.

The remaining honest limit: "the test 835 always pays in full, with the same
charge amounts you submitted" is still vendor documentation plus our single
capture, not something a query can prove. What the query DID rule out is the
most plausible way that could have been wrong — an alternate payer to aim at.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the same conclusion this bead already reached from the
fixture side: rejections are testable for real, adjudication outcomes are not.
A denial, a partial payment, or a contractual write-off can only come from a
real payer, which is PABLO-zpon.

title: Read the allowed amount the payer reported instead of deriving it
description: Service-line allowed_cents is derived as charge minus contractual adjustments. That is wrong out-of-network, under Medicare sequestration, on secondary claims, and wherever a payer uses PI rather than CO. The payer reports the number directly and we do not read it.
design:
The allowed amount is currently DERIVED as `charge - sum(CO adjustments)` in
`backend/app/claims/remittance_lines.py` (landed pablo#1036). That derivation is
wrong in at least four common cases:

* OUT OF NETWORK: the write-off arrives as PR45 with no CO at all, so
  `charge - sum(CO)` returns the full charge.
* MEDICARE SEQUESTRATION: CO253 is taken from the PAYMENT, not from the
  allowed amount, so the derivation understates allowed by ~2%.
* SECONDARY / COB: OA23 carries the primary payer's payment and contractual
  adjustment; the secondary's own CO may be zero. The derivation is meaningless.
* PAYER-INITIATED PRICING: some payers use PI rather than CO for a
  fee-schedule reduction on an out-of-network provider; again `charge - sum(CO)`
  returns the charge.

THE FIX IS NOT A BETTER FORMULA. The payer reports the allowed amount directly
and Stedi surfaces it:

    transactions[].detailInfo[].paymentInfo[].serviceLines[]
      .serviceSupplementalAmounts.allowedActual

which is X12 `AMT*B6`, documented by the vendor as "The payer payment plus any
assigned patient responsibility". `backend/app/claims/responses.py`
`_parse_remittance_line` does not read `serviceSupplementalAmounts` at all.

DECISIONS CLOSED - do not re-litigate:
1. Read `allowedActual` into `RemittanceLine.allowed_cents`.
2. When the payer did not report it, allowed_cents is None - "we cannot say".
   Do NOT fall back to any derivation. A wrong allowed amount is worse than an
   absent one, and allowed is informational only.
3. `patient_resp_cents = sum(PR adjustments)` STAYS as the only number that
   drives a client balance. That one is safe on definitional grounds: the CAS
   group codes are normative (CMS Claims Processing Manual ch.22 - a provider
   may bill a beneficiary only for adjustments carrying group code PR), so no
   compliant payer can contradict it.
4. Do NOT widen this to quarantine or balancing invariants - separate beads.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `RemittanceLine` carries the payer-reported allowed amount, read from `serviceSupplementalAmounts.allowedActual`.
2. `allowed_cents` on a claim line is the payer-reported value when present and None otherwise; no derivation from CO remains anywhere.
3. A test proves an out-of-network shape (PR45, no CO) does not report allowed == charge.
4. A test proves a line with no reported allowed amount reports None rather than a guess.
5. `patient_resp_cents` is unchanged and still the sum of PR adjustments.
6. `make check` passes.
close_reason: Landed in pablo#1038; the derivation is gone and the payer-reported AMT*B6 is read instead

title: Calendar OAuth exchange races the auth bootstrap and burns the single-use code
design:
The Google Calendar OAuth callback exchanges its single-use code from a useEffect in CalendarSetupWizard that fires as soon as `code` is in the URL, with nothing waiting for auth to be ready.

Returning from Google is a full page load. React runs child effects before parent effects, so the wizard's exchange effect runs BEFORE AuthProvider's effect calls initFirebase(). getFirebaseAuth() throws ("Firebase not initialized"), getAuthHeader() catches it and proceeds with no Authorization header (lib/api/client.ts:267-274), and the backend's HTTPBearer(auto_error=True) rejects with a bare-string detail "Not authenticated".

That bare string is why nothing recovers:
- peekErrorCode() finds no `error.code`, so the force-refresh retry (TOKEN_REFRESH_RETRY_CODES) does not fire.
- errorCode falls back to UNKNOWN_ERROR, so the boot-to-login branch does not fire either.
- The effect's .finally() runs router.replace(returnPath), stripping the code, and exchangedCode.current is already set.

The code is single-use, so it is burned. Sibling requests on the same page load (status, consent-options) recover because React Query refetches; the exchange cannot.

Observed on dev: five requests 401'd within 9ms of each other on the return page load (auth/session, saas/features, google-calendar/status, google-calendar/consent-options, google-calendar/callback), each logging `auth failed: UNKNOWN`, then the retryable ones returned 200 about 1.1s later.

Note resolveCurrentUser() already waits on authStateReady() plus up to 1500ms for a restored user — that guard never runs here, because getFirebaseAuth() throws upstream of it.

Acceptance criteria:
- The exchange does not fire until auth state has resolved (useAuth().loading === false).
- A signed-out user does not burn the code: no exchange attempt, no exchangedCode marking, no router.replace stripping the parameter.
- Test covers the mount-with-code-while-loading case and asserts no exchange call is made until loading flips false.
close_reason: Shipped in #1035 (merged 2026-09-10): the exchange waits for auth before spending the code.

title: Decide what to do about each eligibility reject code
description: When a payer refuses an eligibility inquiry it answers with an AAA reject code. We parse those and show the payer's advice to the practice, but we do nothing with them: there is no retry for a payer that is merely down, no input correction for a name or member-id problem, and an enrollment problem looks to the practice like a failed check.
design:
NOT part of the SDK epic - this is product logic and can land before or after
it. Touches `backend/app/claims/eligibility.py` only.

We already parse AAA errors (`eligibility.py:338`) and record their codes
(`:611`). The retry at `:522` is transport level and does not read them. Add a
code-to-disposition table with three outcomes:

RETRY AS-IS (the payer is down, nothing to fix):
  42 unable to respond; 80 no response / terminated; 79 together with 42;
  HTTP 429. Real time: retry immediately, up to about 2 minutes. Scheduled:
  exponential backoff from 1 minute to 30 minutes.

FIX INPUT, THEN RETRY:
  75 subscriber not found - send all available demographics, then try name
     variants (nicknames, accented characters, hyphenated compounds).
  72 invalid or missing member id - strip the `80840` card-issuer prefix. Do
     this at intake capture as well, so the check never fails for it.
  73 name must match the card exactly, apostrophes and hyphens included.
  65, 67, and 56/57/58 (date format, missing required field).

STOP - NEEDS A HUMAN OR AN ENROLLMENT:
  79 alone - unknown or unconfigured payer id. Do NOT auto-retry.
  41 provider enrollment; 43 / 51 provider not enrolled. These must surface as
     an enrollment task on the deployment's own notification surface (see
     `backend/app/claims/events.py`), NOT to the clinician as "eligibility
     failed".

SAFETY GUARD, non-negotiable: an identity-relaxing retry (dropping the member
id, varying the name) must NEVER auto-accept a response whose returned
demographics disagree with the patient on file. That returns a different
person's coverage into a chart. On mismatch, stop and surface for human review.

DECISIONS CLOSED: this logic is deterministic and unit-tested in our code. It is
not delegated to a model at runtime, and we do not adopt the vendor MCP server -
its tools wrap endpoints we already call and it would put a third party in the
PHI path.

CAPTURE IS POSSIBLE WITHOUT A REAL PAYER - corrected 2026-09-09.
Stedi mock payers answer through the REAL eligibility API with a TEST key
(`/healthcare/api-reference/mock-requests-eligibility-checks`), so a response
captured from them is a genuine capture: real endpoint, real serialisation,
real key names and envelope. That satisfies "captured, not authored" for
SHAPE, and needs no payer relationship - the live lane already has the key as
`CLEARINGHOUSE_TEST_API_KEY`.

Scenarios the mocks cover: Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare (active AND
inactive), Anthem BCBS CA and BCBS Texas and Oscar (dependent as spouse / as
child, and the case where the payer returns the dependent inside the
subscriber object), Ambetter and Humana (subscriber only), Kaiser NCal, CMS
(active + MBI lookup), Ameritas and MetLife (dental, service code 35). Plus
canned AAA errors 42, 43, 72, 73, 75 and 79 - exactly the codes the
disposition table in PABLO-os22 has to get right.

WHAT THE MOCKS DO NOT COVER: a behavioural carve-out. No mock payer returns
one, so `PABLO-d8ow.36` still needs a response from a real payer to prove the
carve-out reading. Do not let a mock capture be mistaken for closing it.

So the split is: SHAPE can be proven now against mocks; carve-out SEMANTICS
cannot.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A reject-code disposition table exists with the three outcomes, unit-tested per code listed in the design.
2. Codes 42, 80 and HTTP 429 retry automatically within the stated bounds; code 79 alone never auto-retries.
3. Code 72 strips the `80840` prefix at intake capture, with a test.
4. Codes 41, 43 and 51 raise an enrollment task through the claim-events surface and are not reported to the clinician as a failed eligibility check.
5. A test proves an identity-relaxing retry whose response demographics disagree with the patient on file is NOT auto-accepted.
6. `make check` passes.
notes:
worker exited with PR (open) — office poll tagged pr-open
PR merged (https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/1057) — reconciled

title: Ask a claim what happened to it, instead of polling a transaction feed
description: Three protocol methods exist only to work a transaction feed: poll for transactions, fetch a document by id, then hand raw JSON to a parser. The vendor's claim-lifecycle API returns one timeline per claim carrying submissions, 277CA acknowledgments and 835 payment information already matched to that claim.
design:
Replace `get_transaction`, `list_transactions` and `get_claim_acknowledgment`
(`backend/app/claims/clearinghouse.py`) with claim-lifecycle methods backed by
the SDK: `GetClaimTimeline`, plus `GetClaim` / `ListClaims` where callers need
them.

`get_claim_acknowledgment` currently returns `dict[str, Any]` because there was
no typed shape to return. The timeline has one - a stream whose entries are
`professionalClaimSubmission` | `claimAcknowledgment` | `claimPaymentInformation`.

This retires the `core` polling host entirely (`stedi.py:398`, `:405`).

IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: `claimPaymentInformation` is CLAIM level (one CLP loop:
`claimPaymentAmount`, `patientResponsibilityAmount`, `checkOrEftTraceNumber`,
`statusCode`). It is NOT service-line level. Posting to individual claim lines
still needs the full 835 and is NOT in this bead - it belongs to the remittance
work. Do not widen this diff to attempt line-level posting.

Callers to update: `backend/app/claims/status_worker.py`, `acknowledgments.py`,
`watchdog.py`, `backend/app/routes/claim_status.py`.

CAPTURED, NOT AUTHORED: capture real timelines from the vendor test payer
(submission through acknowledgment through remittance) and scrub them into
`backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/` before writing the parser.

HARD DEPENDENCY FOUND — probed live 2026-09-09, changes the landing order.
The claim-lifecycle API only knows claims submitted through its OWN
submission endpoint. A test account with a long history of claims filed
through the legacy Change-Healthcare-compat path answers `list_claims` with
ZERO claims, and there is therefore no claim id to ask `GetClaimTimeline`
about. Filing one claim through `CreateProfessionalClaimSubmission` made it
appear immediately, with a full timeline (submission + 277CA + 835) inside
about fifteen seconds.

So this bead cannot deliver value on its own: the remittance reader is
correct and tested, and reads nothing, until submission moves to the native
API (PABLO-zz6p.6). Land .6 BEFORE relying on this in production, or the
remit stage polls claims that will never have a timeline.

The reading itself is now proven against a real capture:
`backend/tests/test_claim_timeline_capture.py` replays a captured timeline
through the vendor SDK deserialiser. That capture cannot be regenerated from
the legacy lane, for the reason above.

SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-09-09: the polling host CANNOT be fully retired, and
this bead should not be closed as if it could.

The vendor claim API reports payment at CLAIM level only - one CLP loop
(claimPaymentAmount, patientResponsibilityAmount, checkOrEftTraceNumber,
statusCode). Its OpenAPI has no service-line payment shape at all, and there
is no ERA endpoint on the claims host. The only structured per-line
adjudication is the 835 document itself, reached through
/change/medicalnetwork/reports/v2/{transactionId}/835, which needs a
transaction id from the core polling feed.

So after pablo#1036 the split is:
- DETECTION (was it paid, how much, when) -> claim timeline. Done.
- SERVICE-LINE DETAIL (which session was denied, CO vs PR) -> 835 via the
  feed. Done, in app/claims/remittance_feed.py.

What remains for this bead is the parts that ARE replaceable:
get_claim_acknowledgment and the 277CA path, and get_transaction /
list_transactions where they are used for anything other than finding 835s.
Do not delete the feed wholesale.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `get_transaction`, `list_transactions` and `get_claim_acknowledgment` are gone from the protocol and from the implementation.
2. A `get_claim_timeline` method exists, is typed (no bare `dict[str, Any]`), and pages.
3. No code calls the `core` polling host; its base is removed.
4. A committed fixture is a scrubbed real timeline containing all three entry kinds, exercised by a test.
5. Claim status and acknowledgment handling behave the same end to end as before, proven by the live round-trip test.
6. `make check` passes.

title: Run eligibility checks against the vendor native JSON endpoint
description: We call the legacy `/change/medicalnetwork/eligibility/v3` endpoint and decode raw EB01 benefit codes ourselves. The vendor's own `POST /eligibility-check` (same host, same 2024-04-01 version) returns benefits already sorted into named arrays, with enum network and time-period values and a flag for entries it considers malformed.
design:
Replace `check_eligibility` with the vendor SDK `CreateEligibilityCheck`
operation. Same host and API version we already call, so this is an endpoint
swap, not a version migration.

Response shape changes substantially and REPLACES the decode layer:
  - `benefitsInformation[]` + EB01 codes -> `plans[].benefits.coPayment/
    coInsurance/deductible/outOfPocket/limitations/nonCovered/statuses`
  - `timeQualifierCode` 23/29 -> `timePeriod: CALENDAR_YEAR | REMAINING`
  - `inPlanNetworkIndicatorCode` -> `network.indicator: IN_NETWORK | ...`
  - new `invalidEntries`, which flags payer entries the vendor considers
    malformed (co-insurance with no percent, co-payment carrying a percent).
    We have no equivalent today and currently produce junk for these.
  - `otherOrAdditionalPayer[]` is documented as the coordination-of-benefits
    signal, with the other payer in `relatedEntities`.

Request shape deltas: `tradingPartnerServiceId` -> `payerId`; `dateOfBirth`
`YYYYMMDD` -> ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; gender `M`/`F` -> `MALE`/`FEMALE`;
`serviceTypeCodes: ["MH"]` -> `encounter.services: [{system: "STC", value: "MH"}]`.
Consider sending our patient identifier as `externalPatientId`.

Rewrite `EligibilityRequest` / `EligibilityResponse` in
`backend/app/models/claims_transport.py` to the new shape and delete the EB01
decoding in `backend/app/claims/eligibility.py` that it makes redundant.

CAPTURED, NOT AUTHORED: capture real responses from the vendor test payer and
scrub them into `backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/` BEFORE rewriting the
parser. Do not hand-write fixtures to the shape in the vendor docs. The existing
fixtures were captured from the legacy endpoint and do not transfer.

Do NOT change claim submission or the transaction feed here - sibling beads own
those. Do NOT act on the carve-out detection question; that is its own bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `check_eligibility` calls the SDK `CreateEligibilityCheck` operation; no `/change/medicalnetwork/eligibility` call remains.
2. At least one committed fixture is a scrubbed capture from the real vendor test payer through the SDK, and a test exercises it.
3. `invalidEntries` is surfaced rather than silently dropped.
4. The EB01 decoding made redundant by the typed response is deleted, not left dead.
5. The live lane eligibility tests pass and assert on semantics (a named copay amount, a coverage status), not merely that parsing succeeded.
6. `make check` passes.

title: Run the SDK from synchronous callers, without changing the protocol
description: The adapter is fully synchronous (`httpx.Client`, no await anywhere). The vendor SDK's Python client is async-only. Bridging async to sync per call costs an event loop per call and raises outright if called from inside a running loop, so the protocol itself should become async before any SDK method lands.
design:
ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, 2026-09-09. Do not retry the async-Protocol design.

What was tried: `ClearinghouseClient` and `StediClearinghouseClient` converted
to `async def` (`httpx.AsyncClient`, `acall_with_retry`, which already exists at
`backend/app/reliability/retry.py:167`). That part worked. `poetry run mypy
backend/app` then listed 32 call sites across enrollment.py, submit_worker.py,
status_worker.py, acknowledgments.py and eligibility.py - all mechanical - and
the cascade reached `backend/app/routes/coverage.py` and
`backend/app/routes/claim_status.py`.

WHY IT WAS ABANDONED, and this is the load-bearing fact: the database is
SYNCHRONOUS SQLAlchemy (`create_engine`, `sessionmaker[Session]`,
`sqlalchemy.orm.Session` - `backend/app/db/__init__.py:31,181,280`) and the
routes that call the clearinghouse are sync `def` (e.g. `verify_coverage`,
`backend/app/routes/coverage.py:536`). FastAPI runs sync routes in a threadpool
precisely BECAUSE they do blocking DB I/O. Making them `async def` would block
the shared event loop on every query - a serious regression that no test in
this suite would surface. Async cannot propagate up past the routes without an
