title: Clearinghouse adapter: caller-minted idempotency keys, typed 422/403/409 errors, eligibility error surface
description: The live lane (PR #944) proved three gaps between the adapter and the vendor: the vendor documents an Idempotency-Key header that dedupes a resubmitted claim for 24 hours, but the adapter's docstring says no such key exists and never sends one; 422 and 403 both collapse into the generic unavailable error; and an eligibility check that fails with an AAA error arrives as HTTP 200 with an empty plan status that the response model cannot distinguish from no coverage. Close all three in the adapter, and prove each through the live lane.
design:
Read first: backend/app/claims/stedi.py, responses.py, clearinghouse.py, models/claims_transport.py; the live lane in backend/tests_integration/clearinghouse_live/ (what it proved 2026-09-06) and its conftest; the vendor API reference (https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt index, then the idempotency-keys section of the API reference and the eligibility error docs).

BUILD (adapter only; the live lane is the proof):
1. Idempotency: `submit_claim(req, *, idempotency_key: str)` — the caller mints and persists the key before the call (the submission worker bead owns minting: `<control_number>:<frequency>:<attempt-uuid>`); the adapter sends it as the `Idempotency-Key` header and marks the call KEYED for `backend.app.reliability.call_with_retry`. Update the module docstring that currently says no dedup key exists: same key + same body within 24 h replays the original response (same correlationId), same key + different body is 422 REQUEST_CHANGED, in-flight replay is 409 with Retry-After. Keep a keyword-only parameter so no caller can forget it (mypy enforces).
2. Typed errors in `_raise_for_error_envelope`: 422 -> `ClearinghouseRequestChangedError`, 403 -> `ClearinghouseAccessDeniedError` (enrollment API refuses test keys with 403 access_denied), 409 -> `ClearinghouseInFlightError(retry_after)`; all subclasses of ClearinghouseError; nothing else maps to Unavailable except 5xx/timeouts.
3. Eligibility errors: `EligibilityResponse` gains `errors: list[EligibilityError]` (code, description, followupAction as the vendor names them) parsed from the top-level `errors[]` that arrives with HTTP 200 and an empty planStatus (the AAA 72 case); `check_eligibility` returns it rather than a misleading "no plan status". Unit tests from a recorded AAA response (record one with the test key into backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/ following the README conventions; synthetic member id only).
4. Live lane: extend test_submission_success to call the adapter with the key (not the httpx-level header the lane set as a workaround) and test_eligibility to assert the errors[] surface; keep the shape-diff.

DECISIONS CLOSED: the key is caller-minted, never generated inside the adapter; no retry loop inside the adapter (call_with_retry owns it); enrollment stays untestable in test mode and the lane keeps pinning the 403.
DO NOT TOUCH: credentials.py (landed), validation.py, any worker or route.
Verify: `make lint`, `make test`, and `make test-clearinghouse-live` with the test key exported (all 14+ green). Commits human-written, no bead ids, no AI attribution.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `submit_claim` requires a keyword-only idempotency key and sends it as the header; replay and changed-body behaviour proven by the live lane through the adapter (not a client-level header).
2. 422, 403 and 409 raise their own typed errors; 409 carries retry_after; unit tests per status from recorded envelopes.
3. `EligibilityResponse.errors` is populated from a recorded AAA response and the live lane asserts it for an invalid member id.
4. make lint, make test and the live lane green; no key or member id in logs or assertion output.
notes: PR https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/947; open, CI pending. Adapter: keyed submit_claim (Idempotency-Key, KEYED), typed 422/403/409 errors, EligibilityResponse.errors from recorded AAA 72 fixture. Live lane 14/14 green through the adapter; unit suite 3337 passed; ruff+mypy clean.

title: Run the live clearinghouse suite weekly and on adapter changes
description: The live suite (backend/tests_integration/clearinghouse_live/) proves the adapter against the clearinghouse's test mode but only runs when a key is present. A repository secret CLEARINGHOUSE_TEST_API_KEY (test-mode, never reaches a payer) now exists, so CI can run it: weekly for drift, on pull requests that touch the adapter, fixtures or the suite itself, and on demand. Not on every push: it costs real vendor calls and minutes.
design:
Read first: backend/tests_integration/clearinghouse_live/ and the Makefile target `test-clearinghouse-live` (landing in a sibling branch, work/clearinghouse-live-suite — read that branch if it is not on main yet: `git -C /Users/kurtn/Developer/pablo show origin/work/clearinghouse-live-suite:Makefile`); the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the poetry setup steps and `scripts/ci_classify_diff.sh`; `.github/actions/notify-scheduled-failure` if this repo has one (else mirror the pattern used by the other scheduled workflows here, or omit notification and say so).

BUILD `.github/workflows/clearinghouse-live.yml`:
- `on:` `schedule` weekly (Mondays 10:00 UTC), `workflow_dispatch`, and `pull_request` with `paths: [backend/app/claims/**, backend/tests_integration/clearinghouse_live/**, backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/**]`.
- `permissions: contents: read`. One job on ubuntu-latest: checkout, install poetry the way ci.yml does, `poetry install` in backend, then `CLEARINGHOUSE_LIVE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CLEARINGHOUSE_TEST_API_KEY }}` on the test step only, `make test-clearinghouse-live`, upload the pytest junit/html report as an artifact (always).
- `concurrency: { group: clearinghouse-live, cancel-in-progress: false }` so two runs never submit test claims concurrently.
- The secret is only available to same-repo branches; on a fork PR the step must skip cleanly (the suite already skips without the key — make the job succeed with a visible "skipped: no key" notice, not fail).
- Never echo the key; `set -euo pipefail`; no `tail` masking of the test exit code.
This is a `.github/workflows/**` file: human-merged. Open the PR, state that in the body, do not arm auto-merge.
Verify: `actionlint` if installed (`brew install actionlint` is fine), else a YAML parse; the PR's own path filter will trigger a run on the PR — report its result.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `clearinghouse-live.yml` runs weekly, on dispatch, and on PRs touching the claims adapter, live suite or fixtures; the key is exposed only to the test step and never printed.
2. Concurrency prevents overlapping runs; a run without the key (fork PR) succeeds with a visible skipped notice.
3. The PR's triggered run reports green against the vendor test mode (or the exact failure is in the PR body).
4. PR body states the workflow is human-merged.
notes: PR https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/946; open, human-merge (.github/workflows). actionlint clean. Triggered run https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/actions/runs/34040530300 in flight; expected to fail at make until #944 (suite + Makefile target) merges.

title: Claims end-to-end spec: coverage to paid against the fake clearinghouse
description: Browser proof of the whole claims path on the local harness: file a claim from the unbilled queue, watch the tracker move through submitted, payer accepted and paid on the fake clearinghouse's timers; prove the scrub blocks a bad claim before anything leaves; prove a vendor rejection renders and refiles as a corrected child.
design:
STATE ON 2026-09-10 (read this before the original design below). frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts already exists on main: test 1 (happy path) is written but deliberately stops at "reaches the clearinghouse" rather than "paid", because asserting paid today asserts a known defect (PABLO-1qox: receipts accepted but never matched; PABLO-ukzm: the pipeline's polling stage cannot read the harness's answers). giveCoverage, givePracticeReadyToBill and giveVisitReadyToBill fixtures exist. CLAIMS_PIPELINE_INTERVAL_MINUTES is 1 in docker-compose.e2e.yml. The fake clearinghouse can now produce partial-pay and denial claims and posts 835s off the webhook (PABLO-4emu closed).

WHAT TO DO NOW: (a) write test 3 (vendor rejection -> tracker shows the edit description -> "Correct and refile" opens a child claim carrying the parent's lineage; a control number prefixed REJ-PTR earns the recorded pointer rejection); (b) add a partial-pay / patient-responsibility test using the fake's new partial-pay claim; (c) leave test 1's "paid" assertion exactly as it is unless PABLO-1qox and PABLO-ukzm are BOTH closed when you start -- check with bd show, and if they are, restore the paid assertion from the spec's own git history. Do not weaken any existing assertion. Serial mode stays.

ORIGINAL DESIGN FOLLOWS.

Read first: docs/design/e2e-harness.md (this repo); frontend/e2e/ as landed by the harness bead (fixtures/auth.ts, scenarios.ts, clearinghouse.ts); the claims Billing surface as landed (frontend/src/components/billing/claims/*, the tracker and claim detail routes); scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py control-number rules (REJ-DX / REJ-PTR / REJ-SUB) and its `/_fake/received`.

BUILD frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts (three tests, serial):
1. happy path: `givePatient` -> `giveCoverage` (Test Payer, member id any) -> `giveSessionWithCodes` (90834, one F-code at full specificity, POS 11, rate set) -> UI: Billing > unbilled row shows "File claim" -> click -> review shows no blocking scrub findings -> file -> tracker row reads "Queued to send" (never "Sent") -> within 10 s tracker shows submitted with a receipt time -> within 15 s payer accepted (fake 277CA) -> within 20 s paid with the amount from the fake 835; out-of-band: `clearinghouse.received()` lists exactly one submission for that control number with an Idempotency-Key header.
2. scrub blocks before the round trip: same setup with a category-level DX (F41): "File claim" review shows the blocking finding, the file button is disabled, `clearinghouse.received()` is empty.
3. vendor rejection: force a control number prefixed REJ-PTR through the test hook the assembly exposes (or a DX pointer defect the scrub does not cover) -> tracker shows rejected with the edit description rendered, and the "Correct and refile" action opens a child claim in draft carrying the parent's control-number lineage.
Add `giveCoverage` to fixtures/scenarios.ts (replacing the stub) against the coverage API. Extend the fake if a needed endpoint is missing, in the same PR.

DECISIONS CLOSED: assertions are on what the therapist sees plus the fake's received log; timers generous but bounded; no vendor network.
DO NOT TOUCH: backend behaviour; unit tests.
Verify: `make e2e` green locally; CI e2e job green. Commits human-written; no AI attribution.

HARNESS GAPS FOUND 2026-09-09 BY RUNNING IT. Read this before starting: the
e2e lane itself is healthy (33 specs pass in ~30s against
docker-compose.e2e.yml), but a BILLING spec cannot be written against it as
it stands. Three things are missing, and none of them is in this bead.

1. THE FAKE CLEARINGHOUSE ONLY PAYS IN FULL. `scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py`
   `_build_835_report` is documented as "paying the claim in full for what it
   charged", so no run of the harness can produce patient responsibility at
   all - the exact number a balance spec exists to check. Needs a new
   control-number rule alongside the existing REJ-DX / REJ-PTR / REJ-SUB
   convention, e.g. `PART-` -> an 835 that pays part and assigns the rest as
   PR, and ideally `DENY-` for a denial that leaves the client owing the
   charge.

2. NOTHING DRIVES REMITTANCE POSTING PROMPTLY. The clearinghouse webhook
   (`backend/app/routes/claim_webhooks.py` -> `app/claims/fanout.py`) handles
   277CA acknowledgements ONLY - "an inbound document that is not a 277CA is
   ignored". The 835 is posted by the pipeline's remit stage, which runs in
   process on `CLAIMS_PIPELINE_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (default 5) and is not
   configured in docker-compose.e2e.yml. So a claim reaches paid minutes
   later, well past a 60s Playwright timeout.

   Worth noticing that this is not only a test problem: in production a
   practice waits up to five minutes after a payer pays before the app says
   so. Teaching the webhook to post an 835 the way it posts a 277CA would fix
   both, and is the better fix than shortening the timer.

3. CARD CHARGES ARE NOT EXERCISABLE. There is no Stripe fake in the compose
   stack, so the self-pay half of a balance (a session charge on a card)
   cannot be driven from a browser. The insurance half needs no card, because
   remittance posting writes the ledger row directly - so an insurance-first
   spec is the one that can be written.

SUGGESTED ORDER: fix (1) and (2) in their own PR, then this spec becomes
straightforward. Do not work around them inside the spec with sleeps or by
reaching into the database - a spec that waits five minutes will be deleted
by whoever next runs the suite.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `claims.spec.ts` happy path reaches `paid` on the tracker against the fake clearinghouse with the 835 amount rendered, and the fake received exactly one submission carrying an Idempotency-Key.
2. The scrub-block test proves nothing left the practice (fake received log empty) and the file action is disabled.
3. The rejection test renders the edit description and the corrected-claim action creates a draft child.
4. `giveCoverage` exists in scenarios.ts; `make e2e` and the CI e2e job are green.
notes:
PARTLY DONE in pablo#1056 (4d1cd8bd). frontend/e2e/specs/claims.spec.ts exists and is green, with two of the three tests the design asked for:

  * happy path — givePatient -> giveCoverage -> a coded, finalized visit -> UI: Billing > unbilled row -> File claim -> review shows no blocking findings -> file -> tracker reads 'Queued to send' (never 'Sent') -> the claim reaches the clearinghouse, once, on the native endpoint, carrying an Idempotency-Key.
  * scrub blocks — a category-level DX (F41) leaves the file button disabled and clearinghouse.received() empty.

giveCoverage is implemented against the coverage API, replacing the stub that threw. Two more fixtures came out of it and are worth knowing about: givePracticeReadyToBill (the three identities a claim needs) and giveVisitReadyToBill (codes + a session LINKED to the appointment + a FINALIZED note — 'unbilled' is derived from finalized_at, so a draft note leaves the visit invisible to the queue rather than merely unbilled).

WHAT IS LEFT, and why:

1. The happy path stops at 'reaches the clearinghouse' rather than 'paid'. Not a shortcut — writing it further found two real defects (PABLO-1qox, PABLO-ukzm) and asserting 'paid' today would be asserting a bug. The assertion to restore is in that PR's history. Do it when PABLO-1qox closes.
2. Test 3 (vendor rejection -> tracker shows the edit description -> 'Correct and refile' opens a child claim carrying the parent's lineage) is not written. The harness supports it: a control number prefixed REJ-PTR earns the recorded pointer rejection.
3. The bead's HARNESS GAPS note said the fake only ever pays in full, so no partial-pay or patient-responsibility spec is possible. Still true (PABLO-4emu).

One gap the note did not predict, now fixed in-flight: CLAIMS_PIPELINE_INTERVAL_MINUTES is 1 in docker-compose.e2e.yml. Confirming a claim only marks it ready; the pipeline inside the API sends it, and at the five-minute default no browser test could ever watch a claim leave.
Design refreshed 2026-09-10 (evening pass): a state paragraph now leads, so the next worker starts from what exists (spec file landed, happy path stops at 'reaches the clearinghouse') and works tests 3 + partial-pay instead of re-deriving. Still blocked on PABLO-85ab by the recorded edge.

title: Live clearinghouse suite: prove the adapter against the vendor's test mode, rejects included
description: The recorded fixtures prove our code; they cannot prove the vendor still behaves that way. An opt-in pytest suite runs the same operations against the clearinghouse test mode with a test key: payer search, mock eligibility, the edits that reject on purpose (each asserting our own pre-flight would have caught it), an idempotent success with replay and change, the acknowledgment and remittance round trip through the parsers, and a read-only enrollment check, every response shape-diffed against its recording so drift fails loudly.
design:
Read first: backend/app/claims/stedi.py, responses.py, and backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/README.md (which recording answers which call, and the platform provider record + Test Payer enrollment that ALREADY EXIST — never create another provider or enrollment). Clearinghouse API index: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt; the test-claims workflow page and the idempotency-keys section of the API reference.

BUILD backend/tests_integration/clearinghouse_live/ (pytest; module-level skip unless `CLEARINGHOUSE_LIVE_API_KEY` is set AND starts with the test-key prefix the credential provider recognises — never run with a production key; assert and abort if it does not):
- conftest.py: a `StediClearinghouseClient` built from the env key; a `fixture_shape(name)` helper loading the recorded JSON; `assert_same_shape(live, recorded)` comparing key sets and JSON types recursively (values may differ; missing keys or type changes fail with a diff).
- test_payer_search.py: `search_payers("STEDI")` and `("Aetna")` -> parsed `Payer` list; shape-diff against payer_search_test_payer.json.
- test_eligibility.py: mock eligibility using Stedi's documented mock member ids for active and inactive, plus an arbitrary id expecting the AAA 72 error path; shape-diff against eligibility_271_active.json.
- test_submission_rejects.py: one test per recorded edit rejection (dx_specificity: DX `F41`; dx_pointer: pointer 2 with one DX; subscriber_demographics: subscriber DOB/sex/address omitted with SBR02=18). Each builds the request from 837p_request_test_payer.json with the one defect applied, asserts HTTP 400 / `status == "ERROR"` / the expected `errors[].code`, shape-diffs against the recording, and asserts the local pre-flight would have caught it: today that is `backend/app/claims/validation.py::missing_fields` for the subscriber case; for the two DX cases write the two small pure checks (`dx_at_highest_specificity(code)` and `dx_pointers_valid(pointers, n_dx)`) in validation.py so the scrub bead can adopt them.
- test_submission_success.py: submit the recorded Test Payer request with a fresh random control number (<= 17 chars) and a fresh `Idempotency-Key`; assert `status == "SUCCESS"`; replay with the same key + body -> same `correlationId`; same key + changed charge -> 422; shape-diff.
- test_round_trip.py: after the success submit, poll `polling/transactions` (startDateTime = submit time) until a 277CA and an 835 for that control number appear (timeout 180 s, sleep 10 s), fetch each through the reports endpoints, parse with `responses.py`, assert the 835's `patientControlNumber` echoes ours and `claimPaymentAmount == totalClaimChargeAmount`; shape-diff against polling_transactions_277_and_835.json and 835_report_paid_in_full.json.
- test_enrollment.py: `list_enrollments` for the platform provider id from the README -> the Test Payer 835 enrollment is `LIVE`; shape-diff against enrollment_create_enrollment_835.json (read-only; no create).
- Makefile target `test-clearinghouse-live`; README section "Live vendor lane" mirroring docs/design/e2e-harness.md's section.
Logging/S3: never print the key, member ids or DX in assertion messages beyond the code itself.

DECISIONS CLOSED: opt-in by env var; test key only; the platform provider/enrollment from the README are reused; shape-diff is keys+types not values; no new fixtures are recorded by this suite (if a response has drifted, the test fails and a human re-records).
DO NOT TOUCH: backend/app/claims/stedi.py behaviour (if a live call reveals an adapter bug, fix it in the same PR only if it is a one-line request-shape fix; otherwise file it in the PR body); the fake clearinghouse (separate bead).
Verify: with the key exported locally (`gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=stedi-api-key --project=pablohealth-dev`), `make test-clearinghouse-live` green; without it, the whole module skips with a clear reason; `make check` green. Commits human-written, no bead ids, no AI attribution.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Without `CLEARINGHOUSE_LIVE_API_KEY` the suite skips with an explanatory reason; with a production-mode key it aborts before any call.
2. With the dev test key, all six modules pass: payer search, eligibility (active/inactive/error), the three deliberate rejects, idempotent success + replay + 422, the 277CA/835 round trip parsed by responses.py, and the read-only enrollment check.
3. Each reject test asserts the local pre-flight check (validation.py) flags the defect before the round trip.
4. Every live response shape-diffs against its recorded fixture (keys and types) and the helper fails with a readable diff on drift.
5. No key, member id or DX appears in logs or assertion output; `make check` green; PR open with no AI attribution.
notes: PR https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/944; open, CI pending. Live lane green with the dev test key (14 passed in 82s); skips without key; aborts on non-test key. Adapter drift recorded in the PR body: credential prefix was key_test_ (real keys are test_, fixed here); vendor documents Idempotency-Key (stedi.py docstring wrong; not changed); 422/403 map to Unavailable; AAA errors invisible via EligibilityResponse; enrollment API refuses test keys (403 access_denied) so LIVE check needs production creds.

title: End-to-end harness: compose stack, auth emulator, fake clearinghouse, Playwright fixtures
description: There is one Playwright scaffold with no auth and no way to run in CI. Bugs that reach users live between layers and only a browser driving the whole stack finds them. Build the harness in docs/design/e2e-harness.md: a docker-compose profile with the frontend, the Firebase Auth emulator and a fake clearinghouse that replays the recorded vendor responses, Playwright fixtures in the tiered style, the patients spec rewritten onto them, and the CI job definition.
design:
Read first: docs/design/e2e-harness.md (this repo) — the whole design; implement it as written. Reference material for fixture idioms: the deployed-environment Playwright suites you may have seen elsewhere use tiered fixtures (`onboardedUser` -> `signedInPage` with saved storageState) and API-driven "given" helpers; replicate that idiom here from scratch.

BUILD, in one PR:
1. `docker-compose.e2e.yml` extending docker-compose.yml: `frontend` (production build of frontend/, env from a `.env.e2e`), `firebase-auth` (Firebase emulator, auth only; pin the image tag), `fake-clearinghouse` (see 3). Backend env: `FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST=firebase-auth:9099`, `DATABASE_BACKEND=postgres`, clearinghouse base URL -> `http://fake-clearinghouse:8080`, a fixed webhook shared secret, MFA-required flag off (find the setting in backend/app/settings.py). Health route waits.
2. Frontend: `connectAuthEmulator(auth, ...)` behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST` in the one place Firebase is initialised (grep `initializeApp` under frontend/). One line, guarded; no other frontend change.
3. `scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py`: FastAPI app serving the Stedi endpoint paths the adapter in backend/app/claims/stedi.py calls (read that file for the exact URLs and the fixtures README for which recording answers which call), returning the recorded JSON from backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/. Rules: control numbers starting `REJ-DX` -> 837p_submission_edit_rejected_dx_specificity.json (HTTP 400), `REJ-PTR` -> ...dx_pointer.json, `REJ-SUB` -> ...subscriber_demographics.json; anything else -> 837p_submission_success_test_payer.json; 2 s later POST the backend webhook with a "transaction processed" event for a 277CA and expose the 277CA report; 5 s later the same for the 835 (835_report_paid_in_full.json with the claim's control number substituted). Sign webhooks with the Standard Webhooks HMAC the backend will verify (webhook-signature `v1,<base64>` + webhook-timestamp over `"<ts>.<body>"`). Endpoints `GET /_fake/received` (what it got) and `POST /_fake/reset` for tests. Deterministic; no network.
4. `frontend/e2e/`: `playwright.config.ts` (baseURL http://localhost:3000, `webServer` = `docker compose -f docker-compose.e2e.yml up --wait`, one chromium project, retries 0 locally / 1 in CI, trace on-first-retry); `fixtures/auth.ts` (create the user via the emulator REST API `http://localhost:9099/identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/accounts:signUp?key=any`, sign in through the real /login page once, save storageState; `signedInPage`); `fixtures/api.ts` (bearer client using the emulator ID token); `fixtures/scenarios.ts` (`givePatient`, `giveSessionWithCodes`, `giveBookingLink` — `giveCoverage` lands with the coverage bead; leave a typed stub that throws "coverage API not present"); `fixtures/clearinghouse.ts` (`received()`, `reset()`); `specs/patients.spec.ts` rewritten onto the fixtures (keep the same assertions).
5. Makefile: `e2e-up`, `e2e`, `e2e-down`. `frontend/package.json`: `test:e2e` script.
6. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: an `e2e` job per the design (compose up, playwright, upload report on failure, compose down), classified by the existing diff classifier, NOT required yet. This file is human-merged; include the change in the PR and say so in the PR body.

DECISIONS CLOSED: Firebase emulator, not a fake auth backend; the fake clearinghouse is a separate process, not monkeypatching; Playwright, not Cypress; the existing patients spec is rewritten, not deleted.
DO NOT TOUCH: backend/app/claims/* (the fake mimics them, the backend is unchanged except settings already present); anything under backend/tests/.
Verify: `make e2e` green on a clean laptop with Docker Desktop (`DOCKER_HOST=unix://$HOME/.docker/run/docker.sock` on macOS); `make check`; frontend lint/typecheck. Commit messages human-written, no bead ids, no AI attribution; PR title in plain language.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `make e2e-up && make e2e` on a clean machine with Docker runs `patients.spec.ts` green against the compose stack, authenticating through the Firebase Auth emulator via the real login page.
2. `scripts/fake_clearinghouse.py` answers every endpoint the Stedi adapter calls with the recorded fixture, honours the `REJ-DX` / `REJ-PTR` / `REJ-SUB` control-number rules, and delivers signed 277CA and 835 webhooks on its timers; `GET /_fake/received` lists what it received.
3. The frontend connects to the emulator only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST` is set; production config is byte-identical in behaviour.
4. The `e2e` CI job definition is in the PR (not required yet) and the PR body states it needs a human merge.
5. `make check`, frontend lint and typecheck green; no AI attribution in commits or PR.
notes: PR https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/959; open, CI pending. make e2e-up && make e2e green locally (22/22, 24 s) through the emulator via the real login page; fake answers every adapter endpoint, REJ-* rules, signed 277/835 webhooks, Idempotency-Key echo + replay; make check + frontend lint/typecheck green; e2e workflow is its own file (nightly/dispatch/path-filtered), human-merged, not required yet.
close_reason: BACKFILL. Merged as OSS #959 a5115f0, carrying 4ea5324 'Add an end-to-end harness: compose stack, auth emulator, fake clearinghouse'. Bead was left in_progress.

title: Claim lifecycle events: a listener registry so a deployment can route them to its own surfaces
description: Rejections, denials, stalls, deadlines and enrollment tasks are things a person must act on. Today each claims bead would write its own compliance reminder; that couples every worker to one notification surface and leaves a deployment no way to route the same events elsewhere. This bead adds one in-process event seam in backend/app/claims/events.py, mirroring the credential-provider registry, with the compliance reminder as the default listener. Everything needed is in the design field below.
design:
Read first: the claims code you extend is backend/app/claims/ (clearinghouse.py, credentials.py, stedi.py, responses.py, validation.py), merged today. Mirror the registry pattern in backend/app/claims/credentials.py (_ProviderRegistry + register_clearinghouse_credential_provider + get_...): a module-level registry, a register function, a default.

BUILD backend/app/claims/events.py:
- `ClaimEventKind = Literal["rejected","denied","partial","stalled","deadline_approaching","deadline_missed","enrollment_action_required","unmatched_remittance","paid"]`.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class ClaimEventDetail`: `codes: tuple[CodeRef, ...]` where `CodeRef(system: Literal["carc","rarc","edit","status"], code: str, description: str | None)`; `deadline_kind: Literal["filing","correction","appeal"] | None`; `deadline_date: date | None`; `days_left: int | None`; `payer_instructions: str | None` (enrollment only); `amount_cents: int | None` (paid/partial). Nothing else. No free-text fields.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class ClaimEvent`: `kind`, `control_number: str`, `claim_id: str`, `payer_id: str | None`, `payer_name: str | None`, `state: str`, `occurred_at: datetime`, `detail: ClaimEventDetail`, plus `def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]` for tests and audit.
- `ClaimEventListener = Callable[[Session, ClaimEvent], None]`.
- `register_claim_event_listener(listener) -> None` (appends; document that double registration invokes twice, like register_post_provision_hook in backend/app/db/provisioning.py), `clear_claim_event_listeners()` for tests, `emit(session, event) -> None`: calls every registered listener in order inside the caller's transaction; a listener that raises is logged at WARNING with the listener's qualname and the event kind + control number ONLY (never detail), and the exception is swallowed so the caller's state change commits regardless.
- DEFAULT listener, registered at import: `compliance_reminder_listener` — for every kind except `paid`, upsert one compliance_items row (backend/app/db/models.py ComplianceItemRow; follow the create path in backend/app/routes/compliance.py and backend/app/services/compliance_storage.py) with item_type `claim_<kind>`, label = short copy naming payer_name, control_number (first 8 chars), kind and, when present, the deadline date; due_date = deadline_date if any else occurred_at + 7 days; notes = the code descriptions joined. Idempotent on (item_type, control_number) via a lookup before insert. Register `claim_*` item types with the compliance template registry (see get_template / list_templates_for_edition in backend/app/routes/compliance.py) so the route's allow-list accepts them.
- `emit` must be safe to call with no listeners registered.

TESTS backend/tests/test_claim_events.py: registration order; a raising listener does not prevent the next listener nor the caller's commit (use a real session against sqlite or the test DB fixture the payments tests use); `to_dict()` of an event built from every kind contains none of: "member", "dob", "F41", "subscriber" (assert against a serialised event built from a realistic detail); default listener creates one compliance item and a second emit of the same event does not create a second; `paid` creates no item.

DECISIONS CLOSED, do not re-litigate: events are synchronous and in-transaction (no queue, no thread); detail carries codes and dates only; the compliance reminder is the only OSS consumer; listener errors never propagate.
DO NOT TOUCH: submit_worker/watchdog/remittance (those beads call emit later); any frontend; alembic (no schema change here; compliance_items already exists).
Verify: `make check` in backend (ruff + ruff format --check + mypy app + pytest). Commit message: human-written, no bead ids, no AI attribution. Open a PR against main titled in plain language, e.g. "Let claim lifecycle events reach a deployment's own notification surfaces".
acceptance_criteria:
1. `register_claim_event_listener` + `emit` exist in backend/app/claims/events.py with the ClaimEvent/ClaimEventDetail shapes in the design; mypy clean.
2. Test: a listener that raises is logged and swallowed; the next listener still runs; the caller's transaction commits.
3. Test: `ClaimEvent.to_dict()` for every kind contains no member id, DOB, ICD-10 code or subscriber field (string assertion on the serialised event).
4. Test: the default compliance-reminder listener creates exactly one compliance_items row per (kind, control_number) across two emits; `paid` creates none; `claim_*` item types are accepted by the compliance route's template allow-list.
5. `make check` green; PR open against main with a plain-language title and no AI attribution.
notes: PR https://github.com/pablo-health/pablo/pull/943; open, gates green locally (ruff, format, mypy app, 3321 unit tests). ClaimEvent carries user_id (compliance_items needs an owner and no claims table exists yet). Nothing calls emit yet.

description: Every clearinghouse response the claims work has to read is now captured as a fixture under backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/ (see its README): the synchronous claim accept, three edit rejections, the polling listing with an inbound 277CA and 835, the 835 report as JSON, and the enrollment calls. - Pydantic models, only the fields the claims work reads:
  * ClaimSubmissionResult: status ('SUCCESS'|'ERROR'), vendor_claim_id (claimReference.correlationId), patient_control_number, line_control_numbers (claimReference.serviceLines[].lineItemControlNumber), payer_id, errors (list of EditRejection{code, description, followup_action}), trace_id (meta.traceId).   * PolledTransaction: transaction_id, direction ('INBOUND'|'OUTBOUND'), mode, processed_at, transaction_set ('837'|'277'|'835' from x12.metadata.transaction.transactionSetIdentifier), business identifiers as a dict of element -> value (CLM-01, CLP-01, TRN-02, BHT-03). title: CSP blocks Stripe.js, so card collection cannot mount in any browser
description:
The app CSP blocks Stripe.js, so card collection cannot work in a browser on any deployment. Observed on dev in a headed Playwright run:

  Refused to load the script "https://js.stripe.com/dahlia/stripe.js" because
  it violates the following Content Security Policy directive

The dialog opens, the card field never mounts, and Save card stays disabled because useStripe() never resolves. The e2e failure that reads as a selector problem ("Stripe card number field mounts") is this: there is no iframe to find.

Determined empirically with a local probe page rather than from Stripe documentation, since the last cycle was lost to a selector written from docs.
design:
Add https://js.stripe.com to script-src and to frame-src in BOTH buildCsp functions — frontend/src/lib/auth/firebase/middleware.ts and frontend/src/lib/auth/oidc/middleware.ts. One host, two directives.

Measured, with a control to prove the probe could detect a violation at all:
- script-src: REQUIRED. The live dev run refuses js.stripe.com/dahlia/stripe.js.
- frame-src: REQUIRED. Dropping it from an otherwise-working policy produces
  "CSP-BLOCK frame-src <- https://js.stripe.com" and the element never mounts.
- connect-src api.stripe.com: NOT required for mount. Dropping it changed
  nothing — no violation, element still ready. Stripe.js proxies its API
  traffic through its own iframe, which runs on js.stripe.com and is governed
  by Stripe CSP, not ours. Left OUT deliberately rather than added on faith.

Not proven, and deliberately not pre-emptively allowed: the confirmSetup path and a 3DS challenge (which would render from hooks.stripe.com). Those could not be exercised locally because the deployment publishable key names the wrong Stripe account (separate issue). If either needs a host, the browser says so in one unambiguous line and it gets added with evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] js.stripe.com is in script-src and frame-src in both middlewares
- [ ] connect-src is unchanged
- [ ] The CSP unit tests pin both directives so a future edit cannot drop them
- [ ] make check passes
close_reason: BACKFILL. Fixed and merged 2026-09-05. STRIPE_SCRIPT_SRC and STRIPE_FRAME_SRC now live in frontend/src/lib/auth/csp.ts and are wired into both buildCsp functions - firebase/middleware.ts and oidc/middleware.ts. OSS #919 d4f8329 let Stripe.js load; #920 424d00a added the remaining hosts Stripe documents for Elements. Both are ancestors of 8518340, the base image pinned on pablo-saas main, so the fix is on dev and rides the 2026-09-06 prod promote.

title: Remittance: 835 ingest, auto-post to claim lines, unmatched queue, patient-responsibility rollover
description: Close the loop. When the payer's remittance arrives, post allowed/paid/patient-responsibility and adjustment codes onto the claim lines, move the claim to paid, partial or denied, queue anything that cannot be matched instead of dropping it, and carry the patient's share onto the charge ledger as an amount owed, without copying adjudication detail across.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.
- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

- Table remittances (per-tenant): id, vendor_transaction_id (unique), received_at, raw jsonb (the parsed 835 from the adapter; encrypted at rest with the existing helper), parse_state, match_state CHECK IN ('matched','unmatched','partial'), matched_claim_id, payer_id, check_or_eft_number, total_paid_cents.
- backend/app/claims/remittance.py: ingest(vendor_transaction_id) fetches via get_transaction, stores the row, matches each claim payment by the echoed control number (CLP01) within the tenant; exact match -> post_lines: per service line write allowed_cents, paid_cents, patient_resp_cents, adjustments (group code + CARC + amount, RARC list); claim.total_paid_cents; state paid when all lines paid in full, partial when some, denied when paid 0 with a denial group; no match -> match_state unmatched + compliance reminder "Remittance <check#> references unknown claim". Never mutate a matched claim twice for the same remittance (unique on remittance_id + claim_id).
- Webhook/poll: extend the submission bead's webhook dispatcher for 835 'transaction processed' events; the status worker polls for remittances too.
- Rollover: when patient_resp_cents > 0 on a matched claim, create a patient_charges-side "amount owed" entry (status 'due', no card charge) referencing claim.control_number only: no CARC text, no member id, no diagnosis. Reuse the ledger row shape; do not invent a second ledger.
- UI: claim detail shows per-line adjudication with CARC/RARC codes and their standard descriptions (ship the code tables as data, e.g. backend/app/claims/carc.py); Billing page gets an "Unmatched remittances" list.

DECISIONS CLOSED: auto-post exact matches, queue everything else; the rollover carries amount + claim reference only; remittance raw payloads are financial records with no deletion path in this bead.
DO NOT TOUCH: submission worker internals beyond the dispatcher hook; charge card flows.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-06 (events): after posting, emit through `backend/app/claims/events.py::emit`: `denied` (CARC/RARC CodeRefs with descriptions from the code tables bead), `partial` (same, plus amount_cents = claim paid amount; include one CodeRef per fully-adjusted line so a consumer can tell a soft denial), `paid` (amount_cents), and `unmatched_remittance` (no claim_id; control_number = the 835's echoed PCN). Do not write reminders directly.

NOTE FROM THE EVENTS BEAD (landed as PR pablo#943): ClaimEvent carries `user_id` (the clinician who owns the claim) because compliance_items.user_id is NOT NULL and RLS-keyed — pass it on every emit. The default listener writes in YOUR session, so a worker must run with a tenant-scoped session and `app.current_user_id` armed (see backend/app/db/__init__.py arm_current_user_id), otherwise the reminder insert fails closed and is swallowed: the state change commits, the reminder silently does not. Add a test that a worker-emitted event produces the compliance item.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-06 (patient responsibility, decided by Kurt): the rollover writes ledger rows with the kinds the ledger-kinds bead (PABLO-d8ow.28) defines: one 'contractual_adjustment' row per CO-group amount (informational, never owed), and one 'patient_resp' row per adjudicated claim = PR total minus any 'copay' row already collected for that appointment (floor 0; an over-collection writes a 'credit' row). The claim keeps the gross patient_resp_cents. Balance is computed from the ledger (backend/app/payments/balance.py), never stored. Also: an 835 can arrive with no payer-sourced 277CA before it (the vendor test payer does exactly this), so pay/partial/deny transitions must be legal from ch_accepted and submitted as well as payer_accepted; extend transitions.py accordingly with tests. Depend on PABLO-d8ow.28.

GROUNDWORK LANDED / IN FLIGHT (2026-09-09) - do not rebuild these:
* `backend/app/models/claims_timeline.py` - a claim timeline as domain types.
* `backend/app/claims/sdk_timeline.py` - `timeline_from_sdk` maps the vendor
  SDK answer; `fetch_timeline(client, claim_id)` pages it eagerly (a reversal
  on page two must subtract from a payment on page one).
* `backend/app/claims/remittance.py` - `posting_for(timeline, charged_cents)`
  decides `pay` / `pay_partial` / `deny` plus the amounts. PURE. Nothing calls
  it yet; that is the wiring below.
* Landed in pablo#1028; the rest in pablo#1029.

DECISIONS ALREADY CLOSED, with tests:
* A predetermination is NOT money (`PREDETERMINATION_PRICING_ONLY` prices a
  claim the payer never adjudicated). Neither is a claim forwarded elsewhere.
* Adjudicated-for-zero is `pay_partial`, NOT `deny`: the whole charge went to
  the client deductible, so the client owes it and the claim must not be filed
  away as a loss to appeal.
* A reversal is a negative amount and subtracts; it is never clamped.
* An unrecognised status code reads as "no money moved", never as paid.

THE NEXT STEP, AND WHAT GATES IT:
Applying a posting needs a receipt on the claim, and `claim_events.kind` is
constrained in the database - `CheckConstraint("kind IN (...)",
name="ck_claim_events_kind")` built from `CLAIM_EVENT_KINDS`
(`backend/app/db/models.py`, `ClaimEventRow`). So a remittance receipt kind is
a MIGRATION, not just a Literal edit. Treat the alembic chain as a hub file:
re-point `down_revision` at the CURRENT head when it lands.

IDEMPOTENCY IS ALREADY SOLVED, use it rather than inventing one:
`claim_events.vendor_event_id` is UNIQUE, and `record(...)` takes it. Key the
remittance receipt on the payment entry id (`clp_...`) and a redelivery
cannot post the same money twice.

STILL CLAIM LEVEL. `ClaimLineRow.allowed_cents` / `paid_cents` /
`patient_resp_cents` / `adjustments` are documented as "written by remittance
posting" and stay unset: the timeline carries one CLP loop, not SVC lines.
Line-level posting needs the 835 itself and is NOT covered by the above.

DONE 2026-09-09 across pablo#1029 (timeline reading + claim-level posting +
patient-responsibility ledger row) and pablo#1036 (service-line posting).

- 835 ingest: app/claims/remittance_feed.py scans the feed once per pass and
  parses each remittance; app/claims/responses.py parse_835 already existed
  and had never been called by anything.
- auto-post to claim lines: app/claims/remittance_lines.py splits CAS
  adjustments by group code (CO = contractual write-off, PR = client-owed,
  OA/PI counted in neither) and writes allowed_cents / paid_cents /
  patient_resp_cents / adjustments. Those columns had existed since they were
  written, documented as waiting for an 835, and nothing filled them.
- patient-responsibility rollover: apply_posting writes a patient_resp ledger
  row inside the same branch that records the receipt, so the receipt idempotency
  covers it.
- unmatched queue: NOT built, and no longer needed. It existed to solve
  matching an 835 to a claim; the timeline is per-claim and the 835 is matched
  on the patient control number we set. A remittance line that matches no
  claim line is logged and dropped rather than queued.

NOT PROVEN, and it matters: the vendor test payer pays every claim in full and
emits no CAS adjustments, so the CO-vs-PR split is exercised only against
fixtures we wrote. Group-code meanings are the published X12 standard, not
this vendor. First real payer 835 is what confirms the arithmetic.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Fixture 835s for full pay, partial, denial and unknown-claim each produce the expected line postings, claim state and (for unknown) an unmatched row + reminder.
2. Re-ingesting the same remittance is a no-op.
3. A patient-responsibility amount creates exactly one ledger entry carrying control number and amount only (test asserts no CARC/member id/DX in the row).
4. Claim detail renders CARC/RARC descriptions from the shipped tables.
5. Migration + template regen; make check green.
6. Each fixture 835 outcome emits the matching ClaimEvent with code descriptions and amounts (fake-listener test); unmatched emits `unmatched_remittance`.
notes:
2026-09-06: the Test Payer loop is proven on the live account. Enroll the billing provider with payer STEDI for claimPayment (production key); status goes LIVE in under a minute. A test 837P to STEDI (test key, employerId = the enrolled tax id) yields an INBOUND 277CA and an INBOUND 835 within about a minute via GET core.us.stedi.com/2023-08-01/polling/transactions?startDateTime=... The 835 carries CLP-01 = patientControlNumber and TRN-02 = a remittance trace; the 277CA carries TRN-02 = the claim correlationId. Use those as the match keys.
2026-09-06: retrieve the ERA as JSON with GET https://healthcare.us.stedi.com/2024-04-01/change/medicalnetwork/reports/v2/{transactionId}/835 (277CA: .../{transactionId}/277). Shape verified on a test ERA: transactions[].detailInfo[].paymentInfo[].claimPaymentInfo.{patientControlNumber, claimStatusCode, totalClaimChargeAmount, claimPaymentAmount, patientResponsibilityAmount, payerClaimControlNumber, claimFrequencyCode} and serviceLines[].{lineItemControlNumber, serviceDate, ...}; adjustments in claimAdjustments[] and serviceLines[].serviceAdjustments[] with claimAdjustmentGroupCode + adjustmentReasonCode. Amounts are decimal strings in dollars; convert through money.py.

Nothing fires the 'pay' transition and the Billing Remittances tab is a hard-coded empty state, so today a claim can never reach 'paid' in the running product, however well the rest of the pipeline works. title: Claim submission: outbox worker, 277CA webhook + poll, corrected/void claims, watchdogs
description: File the claim and never lie about it. The claim's state column is the outbox: confirming writes 'validated' and returns; a worker submits from committed state and advances only on the clearinghouse's acceptance; acknowledgments arrive by verified webhook with polling as the backstop; every non-terminal state has a timeout that raises an alert rather than retrying into a duplicate.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.
- Loggable: claim control number, claim state, payer id, vendor event id, CARC/RARC codes. NEVER loggable: member id, subscriber name/DOB/address, ICD-10 codes, any remittance free text. PHI-adjacent events go through backend.app.services.audit_service.
- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

STATE TABLE (implement exactly; each row is a test):
  validated + worker submits, vendor sync-accepts (initial 277CA accepted) -> submitted
  validated + vendor sync-rejects (400 / initial 277CA rejected) -> rejected
  submitted + payer 277CA accept -> payer_accepted (more than 5 days without one -> stalled)
  submitted + payer 277CA reject -> rejected
  payer_accepted + 835 (remittance bead) -> paid | partial | denied (more than 30 days without one -> stalled; the alert names "confirm remittance enrollment is live")
  rejected | denied + human edits -> child claim (freq 7) in draft; void = freq 8
  any + watchdog timeout -> stalled (the alert IS the state; a human resumes)

FILES (backend/app/claims/):
- submit_worker.py: bounded, tenant-scoped scan of claims WHERE state='validated' ORDER BY created_at LIMIT n; builds the 837P from the snapshot (adapter models), sets usageIndicator from the credential mode, submits through call_with_retry with the idempotency class the adapter documented; on success stores vendor claim id + initial 277CA and advances; on rejection stores the 277CA edit findings on the claim and moves to rejected. A crash between submit and commit must not resubmit: write a pending marker BEFORE the call and reconcile on restart by get_transaction, the same pattern as the charge ledger's pending row.
- routes/claim_webhooks.py: POST /api/webhooks/clearinghouse. Verify the shared secret with hmac.compare_digest before reading the body; reject missing/invalid with 401, malformed with 400; dedupe on the vendor event id (unique index on a claim_events table); on a 'transaction processed' event for a 277CA, fetch the document via get_transaction, correlate by control number, advance. Follow the existing payment_webhooks.py shape.
- status_worker.py: poll backstop for claims in submitted/payer_accepted older than 1h without an event; manual POST /api/claims/{id}/status runs a 276 and stores the 277.
- watchdog.py: per the timeouts above, writes stalled + a compliance reminder carrying control number, state and age only.
- Confirm UI: the validate step becomes "Review and file" showing scrub findings; filing writes 'validated' and returns immediately with "Queued to send"; the tracker shows every hop with its receipt timestamp.

DECISIONS CLOSED: state advances only on a receipt; retries never cross a submitted boundary; resubmission reuses the parent control number lineage with frequency codes, never a fresh submit of the same content; alerts go to compliance reminders, not a new notification system.
DO NOT TOUCH: 835 handling (remittance bead), enrollment internals.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-06 (events + deadline ladder): every state change that needs a human is announced through `backend/app/claims/events.py::emit` (lands in its own bead; import it, do not write reminders directly — the default listener already writes the compliance reminder): rejected (with the 277CA/edit codes as CodeRefs), stalled (state + age), and from watchdog.py a deadline ladder: for each open claim call `deadlines.deadlines_for` and emit `deadline_approaching` at 14, 7 and 2 days before the applicable deadline and `deadline_missed` on/after it, once per (claim, deadline_kind, rung) — record the rung on the claim_events table (add `rung` to its unique key) so restarts never re-alert. Copy in the event is code-only per the events design; the tracker (UI bead) renders the deadline from the same function.

NOTE FROM THE EVENTS BEAD (landed as PR pablo#943): ClaimEvent carries `user_id` (the clinician who owns the claim) because compliance_items.user_id is NOT NULL and RLS-keyed — pass it on every emit. The default listener writes in YOUR session, so a worker must run with a tenant-scoped session and `app.current_user_id` armed (see backend/app/db/__init__.py arm_current_user_id), otherwise the reminder insert fails closed and is swallowed: the state change commits, the reminder silently does not. Add a test that a worker-emitted event produces the compliance item.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Each state-table row has a test; illegal transitions raise.
2. A test kills the worker between submit and commit and proves the restart reconciles instead of resubmitting.
3. Webhook: wrong secret -> 401, malformed -> 400, replayed event id -> 200 no-op with no second transition.
4. Watchdog moves a 6-day-old submitted claim to stalled and creates one reminder carrying no patient identifiers.
5. Against the vendor Test Payer with a test key (manual, documented in the PR): validated -> submitted -> payer_accepted observed end to end.

title: Clearinghouse client: credential seam, ClearinghouseClient protocol, Stedi adapter
description: The transport layer for eligibility, claims, enrollment and payer lookup, behind a seam that lets a deployment supply its own clearinghouse credentials, the same shape backend/app/payments/provider.py uses for the payment processor. One protocol, one implementation (Stedi), recorded-fixture tests, no live calls in CI.
design:
SHARED RULES (every bead in this epic):
- Money is integer cents via backend/app/money.py; never float.
- Per-tenant tables ship in the SAME commit as their alembic_tenants revision AND the regenerated tenant template. Tables with a patient_id use the has_patient_access RLS policy; register in the RLS classifier.

- Clearinghouse API reference: https://www.stedi.com/docs/llms.txt (index). Read it before touching the adapter.
- CI gate is `make check` (lint incl. mypy + tests). Run it before declaring done.
- Framing for docs, comments, commit messages: a practice files claims and checks eligibility through its own clearinghouse account. Nothing else.

FILES (new package backend/app/claims/):
- credentials.py: ClearinghouseCredentials (api_key: str, mode: Literal['test','production']) and a provider Protocol ClearinghouseCredentialProvider.get(practice_id) -> ClearinghouseCredentials | None. Default impl reads settings CLEARINGHOUSE_API_KEY (Settings field, str | None). Mirror payments/provider.py exactly in shape and docstring tone so a deployment can swap the provider.
- clearinghouse.py: ClearinghouseClient Protocol with search_payers(query) -> list[Payer]; check_eligibility(req) -> EligibilityResponse; submit_claim(req) -> ClaimSubmissionResult; get_transaction(id) -> TransactionDocument; create_provider(p); create_enrollment(e); list_enrollments(filters). Typed pydantic request/response models in backend/app/models/claims_transport.py. Model ONLY the fields the assembly uses (list below), not the whole X12.
- stedi.py: the implementation. Base https://healthcare.us.stedi.com/2024-04-01. Header "Authorization: Key <api_key>". Endpoints: GET /payers/search?query=&pageSize=10..100 (pageSize below 10 is a 400); POST /change/medicalnetwork/eligibility/v3; POST /change/medicalnetwork/professionalclaims/v3/submission; enrollment + provider endpoints per the docs index. Every call goes through backend.app.reliability.call_with_retry with idempotency class SAFE for eligibility/search/get, and UNSAFE for submit_claim unless you verify in the docs that a resubmitted patientControlNumber is rejected server-side; record what you found in the module docstring. Map vendor error bodies (INVALID_REQUEST_BODY, ACCOUNT_NOT_PROVISIONED, BAD_REQUEST "transaction setting", 429) to typed exceptions.
- 837P fields the adapter must accept from the assembly: tradingPartnerServiceId, usageIndicator (T from a test key), billing {npi, employerId, organizationName, address, contactInformation, taxonomyCode}, submitter {organizationName, contactInformation, submitterIdentification}, receiver {organizationName}, subscriber {memberId, paymentResponsibilityLevelCode 'P', firstName, lastName, gender, dateOfBirth YYYYMMDD, address, groupNumber}, claimInformation {claimFilingCode 'CI', patientControlNumber, claimChargeAmount, placeOfServiceCode, claimFrequencyCode, signatureIndicator 'Y', planParticipationCode 'A', benefitsAssignmentCertificationIndicator 'Y', releaseInformationCode 'Y', healthCareCodeInformation [{diagnosisTypeCode 'ABK'|'ABF', diagnosisCode}], serviceLines [{serviceDate, providerControlNumber, renderingProvider {firstName, lastName, npi, providerType 'RenderingProvider', taxonomyCode}, professionalService {procedureIdentifier 'HC', procedureCode, procedureModifiers, lineItemChargeAmount, measurementUnit 'UN', serviceUnitCount, compositeDiagnosisCodePointers {diagnosisCodePointers}}}]}.
- Tests: recorded JSON fixtures under backend/tests/fixtures/clearinghouse/ for each call (a 271, a submission response with its initial 277CA, an enrollment); httpx mock transport; no network in tests. Add backend/scripts/clearinghouse_smoke.py that takes the key from the env and runs payer search + a mock eligibility + a test submission to payer 'STEDI'. For humans, not CI.

DECISIONS CLOSED: one vendor implementation; the protocol exists for portability, not for a second vendor now; JSON API only (no raw X12, no SFTP); test-vs-production is inferred from the key, never a separate flag.
DO NOT TOUCH: tables (sibling beads); UI; workers (submission bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. mypy + ruff clean on backend/app/claims/ and the models module.
2. One fixture test per protocol method, including error mapping for 400/429 and the unprovisioned-account body.
3. The credential provider seam is exercised by a test that swaps in a fake provider.
4. The smoke script, run by a human with a test key, prints a payer search hit, a 271 with a trace id, and either a submission result or the vendor's provisioning error verbatim.
5. No API key or PHI appears in logs (grep the diff for logger calls).
notes:
2026-09-06, verified on the live account: (1) Stedi does NOT dedupe on patientControlNumber; the same PCN submitted three times produced three claims. (2) The dedupe mechanism is the Idempotency-Key request header (https://www.stedi.com/docs/healthcare/api-reference#idempotency-keys): same key + same body within 24h replays the original response with the same correlationId and creates no second claim; same key + different body returns 422 REQUEST_CHANGED; same key while the first is in flight returns 409 with Retry-After. So submit_claim's retry class is KEYED: the caller mints a per-attempt key, persists it on the claim before the call, and passes it on every retry of that attempt; a corrected claim gets a new key. Always send the header. (3) Edit rejections are HTTP 400 with status ERROR and errors[] of {code, description, followupAction}; map to a typed ClaimRejected exception carrying the errors. 4xx responses are non-billable per Stedi's billing doc.

title: Insurance claims through a clearinghouse: coverage, eligibility, 837P filing, remittance
description:
Let a practice check a client's insurance eligibility, build a claim from a session, file it electronically through the practice's own clearinghouse account (Stedi), track it to acknowledgment and remittance, and post what the payer paid back onto the charge ledger, with every state change driven by a receipt from the next hop and every stall alerted, never silent.

The chart already holds most of a claim: visit codes (CPT, modifiers, units, place of service, ordered ICD-10) live on the appointment; rates resolve from the client and the appointment type; the charge ledger and the unbilled-sessions queue exist. What is missing is coverage on file, the practice's billing identity, the claim assembly itself, and the transport.

Claim lifecycle (state may only advance on a positive artifact from the next hop):
  draft -> validated -> submitted -> ch_accepted (initial 277CA) -> payer_accepted (payer 277CA) -> paid | partial | denied (835)
  any -> rejected (277CA reject) [terminal until edited -> corrected claim]
  any non-terminal -> stalled (watchdog timeout) [an alert, never a retry]

Children, in dependency order: coverage tables (.1), billing identity (.2), clearinghouse client (.3), claim assembly + scrub (.4), biller export (.5), eligibility at intake (.6), enrollment (.7), submission worker + acknowledgments (.8), remittance posting (.9), EOB upload (.10), Billing page UI (.11), plus PABLO-y7u (superbill from the assembly).

Out of scope for the epic: institutional (837I) claims, secondary/tertiary claims, paper claims, any automated appeal. The epic is primary professional claims for outpatient behavioral health.

title: Charging a saved card 502s: off_session is passed on the unconfirmed PaymentIntent create
description:
Charging a saved card always fails with 502. The e2e run on 2026-09-05 hit "502 The card processor rejected the charge request"; Cloud Logging shows POST /v1/payment_intents returning 400, and a direct replay against the test-mode connected account gives Stripe reason verbatim:

  The parameter `off_session` cannot be passed when creating a PaymentIntent unless `confirm` is set to true.

The charge route creates the PaymentIntent deliberately unconfirmed (so the intent id is committed to the ledger before any money can move) and confirms it in a second call. off_session belongs on that second call, not the first. It has been on the create since the original payments PR (#906), so charging a saved card has never worked through the product — the earlier manual $150 charge went through the driver, which confirms in one step.

The payment_method_types[0]=card line added in #914 is NOT implicated: replaying without it fails identically, and replaying with it but without off_session succeeds.
design:
Move "off_session": "true" from the create payload to the confirm payload in charge_patient (backend/app/routes/patient_payments.py). The create keeps amount/currency/customer/payment_method/payment_method_types/metadata; the confirm call, which currently sends data={}, sends off_session=true.

Verified against the live test-mode connected account acct_1UCPjiAnt1oZMJjR:
- create without off_session -> 200 requires_confirmation; confirm with off_session=true -> 200 succeeded.
- same shape with tok_chargeDeclined -> confirm returns HTTP 402, error.code=card_declined, decline_code=generic_decline, so payment_intent_request keeps returning accepted=False and the ledger still records the decline code.

Unit tests: assert off_session is absent from the create body and present on the confirm body, so a move back to the create fails the suite.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] off_session is sent on the confirm call, not on the PaymentIntent create
- [ ] A unit test pins both halves (absent on create, present on confirm)
- [ ] make check passes
- [ ] After deploy to dev, specs/patient-card-charge.spec.ts no longer fails with a 502; the decline spec reports a decline rather than raising
close_reason: Fixed in pablo#917 (merged 2026-09-06). off_session moved from the unconfirmed PaymentIntent create to the confirm; verified against the test-mode connected account (success + 402 decline). Dev deploy and e2e re-run still pending.

title: Availability engine evaluates rules and builds slots in an explicit timezone (UTC default, behaviour-preserving)
description: Step 1 of PABLO-38b. The engine reads weekday/hour/date off UTC datetimes and stamps a literal Z onto rule wall-clock minutes (backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:146-149, :209-214), so since #765 a non-UTC clinician with rules configured is refused for in-hours bookings and sees shifted slots. This bead adds a keyword-only tz to check_conflicts/get_free_slots (and SchedulingService pass-through) with a UTC default so nothing changes until PABLO-38b.2 wires the owner's preference.
design:
Make the availability engine compute in an explicit timezone instead of reading weekday/hour/date off UTC datetimes. Behaviour-preserving by construction: `tz` defaults to UTC, so every existing assertion in backend/tests/test_availability_engine.py passes unchanged; the new tests prove the zone-aware path. Parent PABLO-38b has the full diagnosis (this is a live bug since #765 for any non-UTC clinician with rules configured).

SCOPE: backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py, backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py (kwarg pass-through only), their tests. OUT OF SCOPE: routes (PABLO-38b.2 resolves the owner's timezone and passes it), frontend, recurrence.py (already zone-correct: :52-56, :78), Google sync (google_calendar_service.py:345-352 pushes UTC and stays as is).

VERIFIED POINTERS (main @ 84f9fb0), every site that must switch to local time:
- backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/availability.py:7 imports only datetime/timedelta (add `from datetime import UTC, date, time, tzinfo` and `from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo` only in tests); :20-21 `_parse_iso` parses "Z" as aware UTC (keep); :24-26 `_time_to_minutes` (keep); :58 `check_conflicts(self, user_id, start, end)`; :90-92 `get_free_slots(self, user_id, date_str, duration_minutes=None) -> FreeSlotsResult`; :123-124 day window `f"{date_str}T00:00:00Z"` / `T23:59:59Z` (UTC window — replace); :146-149 slot strings `f"{date_str}T{start_h:02d}:{start_m:02d}:00Z"` (the false Z — replace); :209-214 `_check_working_hours` weekday/hour/minute off proposed_start; :244-247 `_check_block_time_range` same; :262, :291-293, :317-318, :337, :350 `strftime` date/day-boundary reads; :365, :379 weekday from `fromisoformat(f"{date_str}T00:00:00+00:00")`; :465-467 `_appointments_to_blocked_minutes` hour/minute off stored UTC start_at.
- backend/app/scheduling_engine/services/scheduling.py:33-38 `_to_utc` (leave; inputs from routes are aware), :65-85 `_check_availability_rules(user_id, start_dt, end_dt)` → :81 `check_conflicts(user_id, start_dt, end_dt)`; :151 and :234 the two call sites (create, update); :349 recurring reads `recurrence["timezone"]`.
- Tests: backend/tests/test_availability_engine.py:36-39 `_parse_dt`, :87-90 the canonical rule + check_conflicts shape (UTC Z strings). backend/tests/test_scheduling_service.py for the service pass-through.

MECHANISM:
1. `check_conflicts(self, user_id, start, end, *, tz: tzinfo = UTC)` and `get_free_slots(self, user_id, date_str, duration_minutes=None, *, tz: tzinfo = UTC)`. Keyword-only so no positional caller breaks.
2. A single helper `_local(dt: datetime, tz) -> datetime` = `_parse_iso(dt) if str else dt` then `.astimezone(tz)`; every site listed above calls it before `.weekday()`, `.hour`, `.minute`, `.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")`. Per-rule `_check_*` methods receive `tz` (or a pre-localised datetime — pick one, apply consistently).
3. get_free_slots: `day = date.fromisoformat(date_str)`; `day_start = datetime.combine(day, time(0), tzinfo=tz)`; `day_end = day_start + timedelta(days=1)` (exclusive); query appointments between their UTC conversions (:123-124); weekday = `day.weekday()` (replaces :365/:379); slot start = `datetime.combine(day, time(h, m), tzinfo=tz).astimezone(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")` (replaces :146-149; the emitted Z is now true UTC). Blocked minutes from appointments (:465-467) use `_local(appt.start_at, tz)`.
4. scheduling.py: `_check_availability_rules(..., tz: tzinfo = UTC)`; `create_appointment`, `update_appointment`, `create_recurring_appointment` accept `tz: tzinfo = UTC` (keyword-only) and forward it at :151 / :234 and the recurring rule check. The recurring path keeps using the request's `timezone` for EXPANSION (recurrence.py) and uses `tz` for rule checks — they are the same zone in practice once 38b.2 lands, but this bead does not conflate them.
5. Do NOT change: stored rule params, `_time_to_minutes`, `_parse_iso`, FreeSlotsResult shape, the configured/unconfigured distinction from #651, the buffer/max_per_day semantics — only the frame in which they are evaluated.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate: keyword-only `tz` with UTC default (behaviour-preserving; the flip happens in 38b.2); slot strings stay ISO-Z (true UTC) rather than gaining an offset — every consumer already parses Z; day window is local-midnight to next local-midnight, exclusive end; DST via ZoneInfo per-date arithmetic.

MIGRATION: none.

LANE: fleet-eligible — PHI: none (synthetic fixtures) · money/entitlement: none · prod infra: none · auth/RLS: none · vendor dashboards: none · patent-adjacent: none (timezone arithmetic, no known claim surface) · outbound: none.
acceptance_criteria:
1. backend/tests/test_availability_engine.py: every pre-existing test passes with NO assertion changed (UTC default preserves behaviour).
2. New tests with `tz=ZoneInfo("America/New_York")` and a working_hours rule Wednesday 09:00-17:00 (day_of_week 2): `check_conflicts(USER_ID, "2026-08-26T19:00:00Z", "2026-08-26T19:50:00Z", tz=NY)` (15:00 EDT) returns NO hard conflict; `check_conflicts(..., "2026-08-26T12:00:00Z", "2026-08-26T12:50:00Z", tz=NY)` (08:00 EDT) returns a conflict; the same two calls WITHOUT tz give the inverse results (pins that the flip is the tz, nothing else).
3. `get_free_slots(USER_ID, "2026-08-26", 50, tz=NY)` first slot start == "2026-08-26T13:00:00Z" (09:00 EDT) and last slot ends at or before "2026-08-26T21:00:00Z"; `get_free_slots(USER_ID, "2026-11-04", 50, tz=NY)` first slot == "2026-11-04T14:00:00Z" (09:00 EST after the fall-back) — DST handled per date.

Local day window: an appointment stored at 2026-08-27T02:00:00Z (22:00 EDT on the 26th) is counted on the 26th, not the 27th, with tz=NY — a max_per_day 1 rule refuses a second booking on the 26th local and `get_free_slots("2026-08-27", tz=NY)` is unaffected by it; with the UTC default the same appointment lands on the 27th (pins the window change).

6. backend/tests/test_scheduling_service.py: a recording fake engine asserts `create_appointment(..., tz=NY)` and `update_appointment(..., tz=NY)` forward `tz` to check_conflicts; omitting it forwards UTC.
7. `make check` green (ruff, ruff format, mypy-clean annotations: `tzinfo`, not `Any`); no new alembic revision; no file outside backend/app/scheduling_engine/ and backend/tests/ modified.

title: Offload standalone-note dictation generation to the SOAP Cloud Tasks worker
description:
Creating a standalone note WITH a dictation transcript still runs the LLM on the request thread. backend/app/routes/notes.py create_standalone_note (:265) calls note_generation_service.generate_note inline (:348) whenever request.dictation_transcript is present (:336) — 15-60 s per request. The two sibling call sites already moved off the request thread: upload_session persists a PROCESSING session, enqueues /api/internal/jobs/generate-soap and returns 202 (backend/app/routes/sessions.py:236-270, worker at :349-430), and upload_transcript_to_session does the same (:827-868). title: A failed mutation tells the user nothing — non-optimistic mutations have no error path at all
description:
A create that fails shows the user nothing at all.

useAuthMutation (frontend/src/hooks/useAuthQuery.ts) only wires an onError when
the caller passes `optimistic` — it exists solely to roll the optimistic write
back. Every non-optimistic mutation in the app therefore has NO error handling
of any kind, and AppointmentModal renders no error state of its own.

So when booking an appointment fails, the mutation rejects, nothing catches it,
the modal stays open with the form filled in, and the clinician is given no
indication whether the appointment was created. The natural next move is to
press the button again.

Found while investigating PABLO-e1b (a booked appointment never reaching the
calendar). Independent of that bug and worth fixing on its own: silence on a
failed write is worse than the missing refresh, because the user cannot tell
the two apart.
design:
Handle it once, globally, rather than per call site.

react-query exposes a MutationCache-level onError on the QueryClient itself
(frontend/src/components/providers.tsx, where the QueryClient is constructed).
A single handler there covers every mutation in the app, including ones written
later that would otherwise inherit the same silence.

    new QueryClient({
      mutationCache: new MutationCache({
        onError: (error) => { /* surface it */ },
      }),
      ...
    })

Use whatever toast/notification surface the app already has; do NOT introduce a
new one for this. If there is none, render the message through the existing
error affordance rather than inventing a pattern.

DECISIONS CLOSED — do not re-litigate

* Global MutationCache onError, not a per-mutation onError threaded through
  useAuthMutation's options. The point is that a mutation cannot opt OUT of
  being visible by omission, which is exactly how this gap arose.
* A per-call-site override may still be added later for mutations that want
  bespoke copy; it is out of scope here.
* Do NOT change useAuthMutation's optimistic rollback path. It is correct and
  serves a different purpose.
* No PHI in the surfaced message: render the error's own text, never the
  request payload.

WHAT NOT TO TOUCH

frontend/src/hooks/useAppointments.ts — PABLO-e1b owns that file. Keep this
change to providers.tsx plus whatever the toast surface needs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The QueryClient is constructed with a MutationCache carrying an onError
   handler, so a mutation with no onError of its own still surfaces failures.
2. A failing create surfaces a visible message to the user; a unit test asserts
   the handler fires with the error when a mutation rejects.
3. The optimistic rollback path in useAuthMutation is unchanged — its existing
   tests still pass untouched.
4. The surfaced message contains the error text only, never the mutation
   variables or request payload.
5. frontend/src/hooks/useAppointments.ts is not modified by this change.
6. `make check` passes.
